name: Maranatha Chapel
Maranatha Chapel - Encinitas Campus
reviewSummary:
Before we left Maranatha Chapel, we spent over six months trying to meet with pastors, elders, and staff to gain understanding and address concerns we had. We didn’t walk away lightly. We made repeated, sincere attempts to have honest conversations, but those efforts went nowhere.

My family attended Maranatha Chapel for five years and served as small group leaders. Over time we saw a consistent pattern of poor accountability, unclear leadership, and very little transparency. Ray Bentley is still listed as the primary leader years after his passing, and although people say “Ray isn’t the church,” in reality his name and legacy still dominate everything. There is no published elder board, and even long time staff couldn’t name who the elders were. Internships also seem to go almost exclusively to staff children, which reinforces the insider only culture.

The weekend services follow a very producer–consumer model: you are told to “fellowship” for 30 seconds with the people next to you, and then you sit and watch a stage performance. Despite banners everywhere saying “Belong,” there is no membership process and no real path to actually belong.

Financial transparency was a major concern. We had been tithing and developed concerns around the total lack of financial transparency after searching and digging for any public information such as an annual report or budget. When I tried to get basic financial information, I was stonewalled at every step. Calls were screened, emails and messages ignored, and the Business Administrator, George Chial, never responded for a long time. When I finally did reach him, he told me it would take months before I could see a budget. Months — just to look at a budget? Attempts to speak with Senior Pastor Daniel Bentley about governance, finances, and how I had been treated were met with the same firewall.

Small groups and pastoral care were also disappointing. The Growth Groups Pastor, Martin Sanders, was warm every Sunday—shaking my hand, talking about our group, even visiting me in the hospital. But when I reached out during a family crisis, he told me he was leaving for vacation and would follow up afterward. He never did. My attempts to reach him afterward were met with call screening and silence. Nearly a year later he finally contacted me, but it became clear he mainly wanted feedback on a study we had done. When I shared that our group found it campy and shallow, he was visibly offended.

Despite the friendly surface and the “Belong” messaging, the culture feels closed, unaccountable, and resistant to honest questions. After five years—and over six months of trying to resolve concerns—we left because the internal culture simply didn’t reflect what we believe a healthy, transparent, Christ centered community should be. Found Maranatha online during COVID in Aug 2020. Have never looked back and decided to move to San Diego on Sept 2022 to be closer connected with Maranatha. The best church I’ve ever attended. The teachings are proud and filled with so much love and care.

It’s a big church with family vibes. Everyone I have encountered and met since attending weekly service and women’s weekly Bible studies have been so warm. My life has forever changed by learning from the late Pastor Ray via streamed services and his Step Into the Story series, which is now hosted by his son Pastor Daniel Bentley which is a pure joy.

The worship team is a delight. The music hits my soul and brings such joy to my life. Kayla and Jimmy who lead are outstanding in their talent. Kayla’s voice is heavenly.

If you’re looking for a new church, please come and visit Maranatha. It’s an extraordinary community with many events to feel closer connected to the Lord, each other and offers so much foundational support and strength for this day and age.

I have been forever transformed and found my home. God answered my prayers and can do the same for you.

All around 5+ stars and beyond. I have a twinkle in my eye after going through so much loss this year.

Thank you Maranatha and staff. Our family attended and served at Maranatha church for years, investing deeply in this community with our time and resources. However, through the lens of Dr. Henry Cloud’s teachings on organizational health, we have realized that the church is operating as a 'closed system' that avoids biblical accountability.
Despite our years of commitment, when we reached out for pastoral support during a significant crisis, we were met with silence. This is a profound failure of the Law of Responsibility. Scripture is clear that shepherds are to care for the flock (1 Peter 5:2) and 'bind up the broken' (Ezekiel 34:16). Instead, we felt like the 'scattered sheep' described in Jeremiah 23:2, who were not attended to by their leaders.
Furthermore, the church lacks the 'relational property lines' necessary for a safe community:
• No Formal Membership: This lacks the contractual clarity of who belongs to the body and who leaders are responsible for (Acts 2:41, 1 Corinthians 12:12-14).
• No Financial Transparency: Paul modeled transparency in 2 Corinthians 8:20-21 to 'avoid any criticism of the way we administer this liberal gift.' Hidden finances prevent the trust necessary for true fellowship.
• No Public Elder Disclosure: Leaders must be 'above reproach' (1 Timothy 3:2), which is impossible if their identities and conduct are not visible to the congregation they serve.
Dr. Cloud teaches that 'transparency is a pillar of trust,' yet this leadership creates a culture of secrecy. We hope they will move toward the light of truth and accountability so that other families do not experience this same abandonment." Our family has loved and grown in this church for the past 7 years. Big church with a
tight-knit family feel. Lots of programs and ministries for every age. Faith building women's ministry. Amazing children's ministry. Awesome worship. Wonderful friendships. We are blessed and well fed on the Word here. You are going to LOVE this body of believers. A group of Christ-followers who gather to worship and praise, to fellowship through meaningful friendships and tight knit community, to give and serve generously, and to be transformed into the image of God's Son.

The worship isn't some showy performance, it's heart felt and genuine. The preaching has depth bur is also relatable and easy to digest. You don't need a degree in theology to understand the messages.

The pastor is young (mid-40's),so the sermons have a certain energy and enthusiasm to them.

The congregation has a heart for Israel and the Jewish people. They celebrate the Feasts of the Lord.

Come check out Maranatha Chapel, and experience the joy, healing, and presence of the Lord.

When I tried to get basic financial information, I was stonewalled at every step. Calls were screened, emails and messages ignored, and the Business Administrator, George Chial, never responded for a long time. When I finally did reach him, he told me it would take months before I could see a budget. Months — just to look at a budget? Attempts to speak with Senior Pastor Daniel Bentley about governance, finances, and how I had been treated were met with the same firewall.

Small groups and pastoral care were also disappointing. The Growth Groups Pastor, Martin Sanders, was warm every Sunday—shaking my hand, talking about our group, even visiting me in the hospital. But when I reached out during a family crisis, he told me he was leaving for vacation and would follow up afterward. He never did. My attempts to reach him afterward were met with call screening and silence. Nearly a year later he finally contacted me, but it became clear he mainly wanted feedback on a study we had done. When I shared that our group found it campy and shallow, he was visibly offended.

Despite the friendly surface and the “Belong” messaging, the culture feels closed, unaccountable, and resistant to honest questions. After five years—and over six months of trying to resolve concerns—we left because the internal culture simply didn’t reflect what we believe a healthy, transparent, Christ centered community should be. Found Maranatha online during COVID in Aug 2020. Have never looked back and decided to move to San Diego on Sept 2022 to be closer connected with Maranatha. The best church I’ve ever attended. The teachings are proud and filled with so much love and care.

It’s a big church with family vibes. Everyone I have encountered and met since attending weekly service and women’s weekly Bible studies have been so warm. My life has forever changed by learning from the late Pastor Ray via streamed services and his Step Into the Story series, which is now hosted by his son Pastor Daniel Bentley which is a pure joy.

The worship team is a delight. The music hits my soul and brings such joy to my life. Kayla and Jimmy who lead are outstanding in their talent. Kayla’s voice is heavenly.

If you’re looking for a new church, please come and visit Maranatha. It’s an extraordinary community with many events to feel closer connected to the Lord, each other and offers so much foundational support and strength for this day and age.

I have been forever transformed and found my home. God answered my prayers and can do the same for you.

All around 5+ stars and beyond. I have a twinkle in my eye after going through so much loss this year.

Thank you Maranatha and staff. Our family attended and served at Maranatha church for years, investing deeply in this community with our time and resources. However, through the lens of Dr. Henry Cloud’s teachings on organizational health, we have realized that the church is operating as a 'closed system' that avoids biblical accountability.
Despite our years of commitment, when we reached out for pastoral support during a significant crisis, we were met with silence. This is a profound failure of the Law of Responsibility. Scripture is clear that shepherds are to care for the flock (1 Peter 5:2) and 'bind up the broken' (Ezekiel 34:16). Instead, we felt like the 'scattered sheep' described in Jeremiah 23:2, who were not attended to by their leaders.
Furthermore, the church lacks the 'relational property lines' necessary for a safe community:
• No Formal Membership: This lacks the contractual clarity of who belongs to the body and who leaders are responsible for (Acts 2:41, 1 Corinthians 12:12-14).
• No Financial Transparency: Paul modeled transparency in 2 Corinthians 8:20-21 to 'avoid any criticism of the way we administer this liberal gift.' Hidden finances prevent the trust necessary for true fellowship.
• No Public Elder Disclosure: Leaders must be 'above reproach' (1 Timothy 3:2), which is impossible if their identities and conduct are not visible to the congregation they serve.
Dr. Cloud teaches that 'transparency is a pillar of trust,' yet this leadership creates a culture of secrecy. We hope they will move toward the light of truth and accountability so that other families do not experience this same abandonment." Our family has loved and grown in this church for the past 7 years. Big church with a
tight-knit family feel. Lots of programs and ministries for every age. Faith building women's ministry. Amazing children's ministry. Awesome worship. Wonderful friendships. We are blessed and well fed on the Word here. You are going to LOVE this body of believers. A group of Christ-followers who gather to worship and praise, to fellowship through meaningful friendships and tight knit community, to give and serve generously, and to be transformed into the image of God's Son.

The worship isn't some showy performance, it's heart felt and genuine. The preaching has depth bur is also relatable and easy to digest. You don't need a degree in theology to understand the messages.

The pastor is young (mid-40's),so the sermons have a certain energy and enthusiasm to them.

The congregation has a heart for Israel and the Jewish people. They celebrate the Feasts of the Lord.

Come check out Maranatha Chapel, and experience the joy, healing, and presence of the Lord.

name: Maranatha Christian Church (Pompano)
Maranatha Christian Church (Pompano) - Pompano Beach Campus
reviewSummary:
I love attending services at this church. The worship is beautiful, and the preaching is clear, straightforward, and always speaks to our hearts.

The church is very clean, and the people are incredibly welcoming, kind, and friendly. From the moment you walk in, you feel genuinely cared for and well received.

One of the things I admire most about this church is that they don’t constantly preach about prosperity or money, and they don’t spend the service asking people to give. Instead, their focus is on preaching salvation. They are not concerned with asking anyone for money—they are committed to sharing the Gospel.

They follow the example of Jesus, who never charged anyone to heal, save, or set people free. Instead, He paid the ultimate price by dying on the cross for our salvation.

That is the heart of this church: to preach salvation. That is what touched my heart and has kept me here faithfully for so many years.🙏🏼❤️ Can’t speak for the church itself but two believers who go to this church were amazing and following the foot steps of Christ.

I met them at a coffee shop but even then they stayed and listened to my story of my faith.

It’s funny how the world wants to keep us separated but we always find our way to other believers.

May Gods blessing be upon you all that read this. Amen. Many blessings Amazing People Eu amo a maranatha , os irmaos sao muito atenciosos , o culto e uma bencao sempre ... Batizei na maranata quando tinha 13 anos e irei ficar aqui ate a volta do Senhor!

name: Mariners Church
reviewSummary: Known for high-quality production and a very strong 'Family' focus. The teaching is described as 'Practical' and relevant. The physical campus is often noted as beautiful and conducive to community hanging out. 'Rooted' is a key discipleship keyword often mentioned by members.

name: Mariners Church Anaheim
Mariners Church Anaheim - Anaheim Campus
reviewSummary:
This is a great church for people looking to build community with other believers. My children love the kids and junior high ministries. The staff is friendly and serve happily. It is multicultural, so everyone feels like they fit in. They have a service for young adults on Thursdays too. We adults mostly view the sermon on a screen, and it is definitely worth the listen. I have learned so much in my year here so far. Sometimes our campus pastor teaches live too, which is also a great experience. The worship is awesome! My favorite thing has been the Rooted program which helped us make really great friends there. Mariners is a great bible based church with a huge heart and love for the community. Mariners Anaheim is a new campus, and it's definitely worth the visit if you are looking for a new home church. It is a growing congregation filled with friendly and loving people, volunteers, and staff. Everyone is welcome with zero judgment! They also have a great children and teen ministry, which means you can enjoy the service knowing your children are safe, and having a great time learning about God in a personalized way. If you are looking for a place to build a community, I encourage you to check out this church. It helped me to Believe again when I wasn't sure.
The only Church to go to if  you've lost, or feel you've lost,  your Faith in the Lord. It's where I want to be on a Sunday and if I could be every day.
Munyoki is The Best. Real and Honest.
Thank you for what you've done for me. Being a member and volunteer at Mariners Anaheim has truly blessed my life. This church doesn’t just teach God’s Word—it equips you to live it every day. The pastors and leaders genuinely care about helping us grow spiritually and give us the tools to serve with purpose. Volunteering here has helped me use my gifts to make a real difference, and I’m so grateful to be part of this loving, Christ-centered community. ❤️ I love Mariners Anaheim! The heart of my church is simple but powerful: to help people encounter the love of Jesus in everyday life and grow deeper as His disciples. The messages are “Rooted” in God’s Word and speak to real life. The Pastors, staff  and church community leave you feeling loved, encouraged, and inspired to live out your faith Monday through Sunday. If you want to be part of a community that passionately pursues God, cares deeply for people, and equips you to follow Jesus wholeheartedly, come visit Mariners Anaheim. It’s not just church — it’s family.

name: Mariners Church Huntington Beach
Mariners Church Huntington Beach - Huntington Beach (North) Campus
reviewSummary:
So I’ve been going to mariners for a long time I love going to Thursday night or young adults worship night. We usually go to the Irvine location, but we’re very close to the Huntington Beach location so I decided to start going there and giving it a try because they have started having Thursday nights. I’m a single mom and I’ve brought my son with me before and I know that technically he’s not allowed in service and they don’t have childcare on that day either but at least at the Irvine location they’re still welcoming and they have a outdoor worship area. I’ve never felt more unwelcome at any church more than this location.  I’ve been to this Huntington Beach location several times I just signed up for a class there to help me with sobriety and I wanted to take my next step in my faith and start serving, but after what we went through tonight during service, they said something about us sitting in the middle or sitting up close because I had my son with me, we moved, and someone else came up to us while we were worshiping and told us to move further back. My son and I were just standing there worshiping he wasn’t disturbing anyone and I told them that I’m not wearing my glasses and I can’t see. And me and my son had already moved back a little bit and out of the center. We were just standing there worshiping, and another person came up to us and told us that we needed to move to the back and that kids aren’t allowed. I never felt more unwelcome at any church more than this one. As Christians, we are supposed to bring people closer to God and into the kingdom. I think it’s important that we raise kids within the faith and start them young, but instead they made me feel welcomed and pushed me away from God and now I don’t even want to go to the class or volunteer there after what happened—we just left after that. You never know what people are going through or what type of day they had. I was already emotionally overwhelmed today so after what happened I wasn’t really in the mood to worship anymore after being treated like that. Mariners itself is actually a really good church but if you do give it a try, I recommend the Irvine location or any other location besides this one. As Christians, we should be happy and welcome everyone and bring people close that our Christ not push them away. I was in praise and worship bands for 20 years or so at various churches. And we worked very hard to keep the worship focused on God and not on our performance. we should be perfuming not performing, perfuming the air with the incense of worship and praise.So what’s with all the Hollywood type search lights thing going on the stage?
Looks like a movie premiere or something.
A far cry from Sweet Hour of Prayer. My first time and it was wonderful. It was alive with happy music and an inspiring sermon. I agree with everyone's statements about this mega church. All they care about is making money. The Pastor in Irvine is so full of himself that he does every sermon and puts it on video so every mariners church has to watch him. He's not the only pastor each church has one but what is there role in anything. Also most importantly for a mega church they really don't help anybody physically or spiritually. We attended for over 5 years and when my daughter needed help they did help about 4 years ago. Now when she needs assistance she was told they only help once in a lifetime. Well thank you we won't need your help when we're in heaven. Jesus says help the poor and needy. Absolutely stay away from Mariners church they obviously do not believe in this. This church in HB has a unique ambiance of faithful, friendly people.

name: Mariners Church Irvine
Mariners Church Irvine - Irvine (University) Campus
reviewSummary:
My wife and I have been going to Mariners Church in Irvine since 2021, and we really love it here. We tried a few other churches before, but this one just felt like home. Even though it’s a big church, it still feels personal. People are friendly, the volunteers are kind, and we always feel welcomed.

We love Pastor Eric (and the whole community around him). He’s faithful to the Word and his sermons are easy to understand and engaging. Every message points back to Jesus and challenges us to grow in our faith.

The church has all kinds of ways to connect. Bible studies, theology classes, men’s/women's gatherings, the Rooted program, marriage nights. We’ve made some great friends here and found our little community inside the bigger church.

Our two-year-old girl loves coming here too. The kids’ program is awesome, and it’s such a gift knowing she’s learning about Jesus from an early age.

Most of all, I can honestly say I’ve felt God’s presence here. The Spirit as at work. The preaching has shaped my walk with Christ, and I’ve seen real fruit in my life because of it. No church is perfect, but from what I've seen I believe Mariners is faithful to the Word, and that’s what matters most to me.

If you’re looking for a church or maybe just curious about God, come visit. You’ll be welcomed, encouraged, and reminded how real Jesus is. Mariners Church in Irvine is one of the most stunning wedding venues I’ve had the privilege of photographing. The campus is beautifully designed, with open spaces, modern architecture, and natural light that makes every moment feel timeless. The main sanctuary is spacious yet warm, creating an intimate setting even for larger gatherings. Couples also love the outdoor areas, which provide gorgeous backdrops for portraits and candid moments alike.

From a photography perspective, the layout of Mariners makes it easy to capture both grand ceremony shots and quiet, emotional details. The staff is welcoming and organized, which allows the day to run smoothly for everyone involved. It’s always a joy to work here, and every time I return I’m reminded why this church is so highly regarded in Orange County.

— Written as a professional photographer with PrinceWeddings.net, Orange County photographer. I spent some years searching for a church that felt like home. I was living in Huntington Beach and heard about the Rooted program at Mariners, along with the first “How to read the Bible” course. Christine Caine was speaking there one evening so I decided to go. She was absolute amazing! So o decided to sign up for Rooted and the Bible course. I started attending services every Sunday and actually looked forward to going to church! And still do to this day! I now live in Norwalk and my boyfriend and I make the drive! We even bring his two young sons and they enjoy the children’s program.

I am so grateful for Mariners. I understand the message that is being delivered, they are not judgmental, but real in they was they delver God’s word. I read a review (the only 1 star review on here) saying they were judgmental and I have never ever experienced that. I know the same goes for so many of the people I have met at this church. It truly feels like home. Like God has His full blessings over this community. Mariner's Irvine hosted Dadfest in honor of Father's Day. Such a wonderful event and sense of community and purpose.

Great food, music, and fun, too.

The church spreads across a park-like campus. A little disorienting at first for newcomers. Still, the staff and volunteers gave warm welcomes.

Returned for worship. Fantastic experience. Appreciated the message, in particular, and how Pastor Eric explained Romans 28:8 in a way never shared before and connected it to the series being taught on Genesis. Brilliant!

Two bonuses: a terrific bookstore and cafe. (Get the chorizo and egg burrito.) ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Every time we visit California, we make it a point to attend Mariners Church in Irvine, and it’s always such a blessing! This past Christmas was especially memorable. The energy, the warmth, and the presence of God were palpable throughout the entire experience.

The church grounds are beautiful and so inviting, creating the perfect setting to connect with the community and feel at peace. The Christmas show and sermon were nothing short of amazing—well thought out, deeply inspiring, and filled with the spirit of the season. The message truly resonated with us and left a lasting impression.

There’s something so special about Mariners Church. It’s a place where you can feel God’s love and the strong sense of unity among everyone there. We absolutely adore this church and look forward to attending every time we’re in California. Highly recommend it to anyone looking for a meaningful and uplifting worship experience!

name: Mariners Church Mission Viejo
Mariners Church Mission Viejo - Laguna Niguel Campus
reviewSummary: We're thrilled to have discovered this church conveniently located near our home. Their recent grand opening was truly divine; the warmth and hospitality we encountered felt like a gift from God. From the friendly faces we met to the welcoming demeanor of the pastor and his wife, every interaction filled us with the Holy Spirit. Now, through Mariners communications platform, we're constantly kept in the loop about church events and opportunities to get involved. Joining this vibrant, Jesus focused, community isn't just an invitation; it's a chance to be part of a movement dedicated to transforming the world in the name of Jesus Christ. Don't let this amazing opportunity pass you by. As a new person to this church I was quickly welcomed in, and approached by several women to make me feel at home. Before attending there I joined their small group called Rooted which was a great intro to get to know people and be involved. The church is great because it is smaller, which I like, because it delivers a more intimate setting and the pastor is very approachable and involved with everyone that attends. Such an awesome church. A place I now call home, have gotten rooted, grounded, love my new church. The worship, word, and fellowship are balanced and intentional. Love our Church Friendly Community Service. Mariners Mission Viejo Church is so welcoming and friendly.  They genuinely care about everyone who attends.  It makes you want to get involved.

name: Mariners Church Mission Viejo - Mission Viejo Campus
reviewSummary: We're thrilled to have discovered this church conveniently located near our home. Their recent grand opening was truly divine; the warmth and hospitality we encountered felt like a gift from God. From the friendly faces we met to the welcoming demeanor of the pastor and his wife, every interaction filled us with the Holy Spirit. Now, through Mariners communications platform, we're constantly kept in the loop about church events and opportunities to get involved. Joining this vibrant, Jesus focused, community isn't just an invitation; it's a chance to be part of a movement dedicated to transforming the world in the name of Jesus Christ. Don't let this amazing opportunity pass you by. As a new person to this church I was quickly welcomed in, and approached by several women to make me feel at home. Before attending there I joined their small group called Rooted which was a great intro to get to know people and be involved. The church is great because it is smaller, which I like, because it delivers a more intimate setting and the pastor is very approachable and involved with everyone that attends. Such an awesome church. A place I now call home, have gotten rooted, grounded, love my new church. The worship, word, and fellowship are balanced and intentional. Love our Church Friendly Community Service. Mariners Mission Viejo Church is so welcoming and friendly.  They genuinely care about everyone who attends.  It makes you want to get involved.

name: Mariners Church Oceanside
Mariners Church Oceanside - Oceanside Campus
reviewSummary: Love the services here. Everyone is nice and friendly and makes you feel welcome and right at home. Pastor and staff are very nice and friendly. They just launched their food pantry on Saturdays for those in need of assistance with groceries/household essentials. Mariners Church Oceanside is an inviting sanctuary that warmly welcomes everyone to be part of its vibrant community. Join us for our three uplifting services at 8:30, 10:00, and 11:30, where our incredible worship team and inspiring sermons from Pastor Eric Geiger create an atmosphere of joy and connection. Be sure to visit our charming Bookstore/Boutique, open on Sunday and Monday from 10:00 to 2:00, where every purchase contributes to meaningful Community Outreach. Experience the beauty of a diverse community rooted in the love of God, family, service, and outreach. We can’t wait to welcome you! Mariners Church has been such a blessing to my family and I. The worship and messages are clear and easy to understand. I really like the breakdown of the messages. The worship music is inspirational and has enabled me to love and play music again. Everyone is very kind and open. You truly feel the presence of the Lord. Mariners Church has pastors that are true shepherds of the church (the people) and partners who will remember you by name and face. If you are looking for a church that is willing to discuss sensitive issues and always remind us that we were all created in the image of God and learn about why Jesus, Come and See! Awesome Black artshow/gallery festival. Beautiful property's great people

name: Mariners Church Santa Ana
Mariners Church Santa Ana - Santa Ana Campus
reviewSummary:
Just seen video on Instagram about this place. Some very nice people in the video but some very sour people here aswell. Maybe the pastor needs to teach love and how to treat your neighbors, you dont just call the police on someone just because they have a camera. Will never attend this place. I’ve always loved Mariners Church and believe it is a great church overall, but I recently had an experience in the Mariners Kids section that left me uneasy and uncomfortable.

When I went to pick up my son, I was waiting for a volunteer to collect my pickup sticker. During that time, my son came out looking noticeably sad, which concerned me. When the volunteer, Leslie, came to get my badge, she called my son over and asked me how old he was. After I answered, she commented in a condescending tone that he had a hard time sitting down/ sitting still.

I responded that he is a kid and he’s excited to be here. While I can’t say for certain how my son was treated while in her care, the interaction made me uncomfortable. I’m not willing to risk my child being under the care of someone who appears to lack patience with excited children.

I still believe Mariners Church is a great place, but because of this experience, I no longer feel comfortable having my son attend the kids’ area upstairs, and I won’t be returning.

I hope this feedback helps bring awareness to how important tone and patience are when working with children. Mariners Santa Ana is an amazing church! Welcoming to everyone, great music, and the sermons are Bible based. I love that this church cares about community and helping people grow in their relationship with God. If you have a heart for Santa Ana and Jesus or Jesus and Santa Ana or whichever then this is a place you need to be.

They love the lost, tired, weak, weary and it's clear with what they do rather than just what they say that they're legit for Jesus here. Awesome Word of God and Spirit lead church. Welcoming, caring, and loving people of God loving on the community of Santa Ana and beyond. Bless to be apart of an amazing humble, God loving team! Btw Lead pastors Guillermo and Nidia Gonzalez are the most wonderful sincere people I have ever met! #ImHome #MarinersSantaAna

name: Mary, Star of the Sea Catholic Church
Mary, Star of the Sea Catholic Church - La Jolla Campus
reviewSummary:
A peaceful, sacred gem by the Pacific.
Mary Star of the Sea is a beautiful, historic church with a serene presence overlooking the ocean. The architecture reflects timeless grace, and the gentle sea breeze adds to the sense of calm and reflection. Whether you’re attending Mass or simply stopping by, it’s a spiritually uplifting place to pause, pray, and take in the natural beauty around you. Mary, Star of the Sea is a visually impressive and spiritually nurturing landmark. Its mission-inspired architecture, intricate mosaics, and vibrant community life are emblematic of La Jolla’s coastal, cultural, and historical identity. Daily Masses are held at 8 AM (weekdays) and Saturday at 9 AM, with vigil and Sunday services offered in English and Spanish In my quest to visit every Catholic Church in San Diego county, I visited Mary, Star of the Sea. Loved how special this church is, just beautiful. Very welcoming in the 7:30 service.  Also, was near great breakfast places. Gorgeous church with one of my favorite Marian images. I've attended Mass and just stopped in to make a visit many times when visiting La Jolla. Beautiful  church.

name: Mater Dei Catholic Church
Mater Dei Catholic Church - Chula Vista Campus
reviewSummary: Mater Dei Catholic Parish Church in Chula Vista is where I go for my spiritual growth and spiritual awakening during service or mass. Cordial and friendly!  very good atmosphere to pray, reflect and thank our Lord for all the blessings received!🙏 My family has attended here a few times. It seems like it is mostly made up of cultural Catholics who lack reverence.  I usually leave feeling disappointed and wishing for a deeper experience with Jesus. Also, as soon as you walk in people greet you by handing you envelopes for offerings. Huge turn-off. Our family ended up making Santa Sophia in Spring Valley our home even though we live close to Mader Dei. I really enjoyed the holy mass. It’s a very spacious temple with lots of light and  two big screens to easily  follow the ritual. It was everything well organized.  Thank you. The concave design of the Church resembles an opera house or a Roman Theater, where all the parishioners have the altar right in front of their visual field.  The floor plan has an inclination of about 6 degrees where the altar is located at the bottom and the entrance is at the top.  This causes the rows to descend until the last row is at the same level as the altar. People in the row in front of yours, can't block your view of the altar. The floor plan helps the congregation to become one and the whole view is spectacular.  Add to this an experienced father who makes the ceremony a beautiful and inspiring experience and you have one of the best places to attend Sunday mass with your family.

name: Mayflower Congregational Church
Mayflower Congregational Church - Aliso Viejo Campus
Mayflower Congregational Church - Lake Forest Campus
Meadowlark Community Church
Meadowlark Community Church - San Marcos Campus
reviewSummary: Since daybreak has come in, my wife and i were positively optimistic of our yearly Easter service for 2026. Unfortunately we were wrong, no stain glass, no old Church hymns, no wooden pews, just modern. My wife i understand that things change. Well, that also means we need to change as well, to a classic old fashion church. If you have a family, this is for you. Not for myself or my wife Meadowlark Church feels like family. It's a God and Christ centered, Bible-based church with pastors and a staff who genuinely care about teaching God's word, the congregation and our community. Meadowlark is small enough to know your name, yet big enough to meet the diverse needs of individuals and families. Meadowlark offers both contemporary and traditional Services, programs for children and teens, background-checked nursery care, midweek Bible study small groups for youth and adults, and a midweek youth group led by an incredibly dedicated and motivating youth pastor. Meadowlark also offers Divorce Care for both adults and children. We are so blessed to have found this church and church family. A beautiful church. A great church to be a part of that is very community friendly. An old friend of mine AL Dovido went there for many years and love the place. him and his grandson build a gazebo there that is still there. The pastor is very nice and humble. A great local church! I Love our Meadowlark Church! A very friendly & loving family church with many wonderful faith based events for all. Inspiring Sermons and music at both the Contemporary and Traditional Services. When my husband and I found Meadowlark Church, we knew we were home!  The people are friendly and loving.  The teaching is from the Bible, the music is great, and Jesus Christ is Lord.  We love our church!

name: Media City Church
Media City Church - Burbank Campus
reviewSummary: I love Media City Church! I have been a member for just over a year now and I cannot express the love I feel from this MCC family! The Lord has worked so many miracles already this year and I know it is due to our continuous fellowship and prayer! Thank you Pastor Billy and Pastor Kristen for leading such an amazing church! Thank you for all our leaders and community outreach families! May our Lord continue to bless Media City Church and all who serve within it! The worship, the message, the community, the youth program...all of it worth your time on a Sunday.  Pastor Billy has a special gift, and the youth program is a second home to my children.  I’m so thankful to have found a church home for my family. I love the community at the church.  The people make you feel warm and welcome during your time at the church.  Connect to a small group really helps with building lasting friendships. MCC is a great place to meet wonderful people, to hear inspiring sermons, and to feel God's presence. This is truly a special church. I loved my Church Family! Pastor Billy has a message for everyone he is truly  anointed by God!

name: Melbourne Church of Christ
Melbourne Church of Christ - Melbourne Campus
reviewSummary:
My grandmother and I have had horrible experiences with their food pantry workers! A FEW of the women that help with their food pantry have just been SO rude to myself and my grandmother! They treat us like we're trying to steal from them, they are so nasty and quick to get onto you about any little thing they can! They are not helpful and they are just so quick to be so rude ! If they are volunteering, I have NO IDEA why! And if they ARE getting paid, then STOP paying them! Im not too worried about myself but I don't understand why they treated my elderly grandmother so poorly! They have terrible attitudes! Besides those few women, others have been great, helpful and nice and all the men have always been helpful gentlemen! Loved attending worship here while visiting friends in Melbourne this week. The pastor is awesome. He is a younger pastor with an excellent ability to reach the family. The song leader was absolutely wonderful. They were all so passionate about doing their part in worshipping Christ. The rest of the church family was incredibly welcoming and friendly. It is a large building so there is plenty of room for more people to join in a really wonderful church. I can't wait to bring my wife down hopefully after Christmas.
If any of you ever visit Washington PA area. We would love for you to join us in worship as a part of our family. Beautiful church . There is a food pantry on Tuesdays from 9-11 am . Anyone who is in need of a little bit of dry goods and clothes are welcome to come.  The volunteers are so cheerful and always have a smile on their face. My son has his boy scout meeting here. I haven't been to a church meeting here, but I  can tell you about the building. The church is very large, the meeting rooms are spacious, the bathrooms are nice and clean. As far as the main room, it's very large with plenty of seating. There's even tables in there for events. I went for the free food and toys they were giving out to members in the community. I was impressed with the care and help they provide but very disappointed in the people who were there taking advantage but acting rude instead of greatful for any help. Thanks to all the kind wonderful souls who donated there time and items so people in need can have. This place is a regular food bank for the needy. God bless all of you.

name: MELBOURNE COMMUNITY CHURCH
MELBOURNE COMMUNITY CHURCH - Melbourne Campus
reviewSummary:
I enjoyed my visit to Melbourne Community Church this morning! They are tucked in the strip mall at the corner of 192 and Wickham Road behind the Walgreens.

Great community of believers and great message about the purpose of prayer by Pastor Brandon Harris who joined as the church’s teaching pastor in 2022. The church was founded in 2002 and longtime worship pastor Walter Staub, ordained by MCC in 2003, still leads the congregation in worship today including some of his original songs.

Beautiful, faithful church here! Amazing church that absolutely lives up to their name. It really is centered around the community, and you'll feel so welcome if you stop in. Pastor Brandon is phenomenal and the worship team truly is next level.

If you're looking for a church experience that's personal and genuine, I highly recommend checking out MCC. I've been a member of this church for the last few years. One of the est things that ever happened to me. :-) Pastor Curt is a teaching pastor. . I'm learning so much from the Bible. The praise and worship team is awesome. And there's a lot of original songs. I could go on and on about how much I love this church. Come learn about Jesus. :-) Pastor Brandon delivers the Gospel message straight on.  Going through the Bible book by book... Brandon has insights I haven't considered due to translation from Greek or Hebrew. A message where Jesus is the focus as the Son of God, Savior and Redeemer of our sins. A wonderful experience in a small community Church. Great homey experience with a Pastor who reads scripture and compared them to current events. It is close net and an experience we look forward to each week

name: Memorial Drive United Methodist
reviewSummary: A traditional Methodist church along Memorial Drive offering community-centered worship and family programming.

name: Memorial Drive United Methodist Church
Meridian Baptist Church
Meridian Baptist Church - El Cajon Campus
reviewSummary: Pastor Rolland and the church family at Meridian Baptist Church are wonderful. It’s a great church that truly feels like a family—welcoming, caring, and full of genuine faith. Grateful to be part of such a loving community. This church has the biggest heart. They have the first Amikas home. At 8x12’ with a 4x12 patio, it’s totally just what a small family could use to get back on their feet. There needs to be more of these all over San Diego. My kids and I struggled for YEARS in El Cajon and are still struggling nearby. We got no help, we got no shelter. Nice that this church selects certain people to be assisted but the others they leave stranded, struggling and to drown don't deserve it. Sad they only care about a few families here and there and leave other to be separated, harmed, or dying. We’ll laid out and supplied small transition homes for the homeless.  More churches and nonprofit organizations should look to this model to help the unhorsed in San Diego County. Great small church. Pastor Rolland is so approachable and gives a great message straight from the bible. All the people are so friendly and the music is always good.

name: Mesa Church
Mesa Church - Costa Mesa Campus
reviewSummary:
Mesa.Church welcomes our community. You!!! Come enjoy Biblical preaching by Pastor Keith Robinson, explosive Christian Worship, holy communion, baptism, fellowship, small groups, missions, children’s ministry, out reach, men’s breakfast and women’s night out. A blessed, enjoyable, friendly local Christian church.
Worshiper for last 5 years.
Pastor Kieth is everything that Worshippers are looking for:
- comforting
- thought provoking
- caring
- educational
- positive effective leader
- humorous
- smart
- charismatic
- organized and well prepared
In short: Pastor Kieth charges-up ⚡️your feelings and awareness of being blessed by God.
The church is:
- very friendly
- family oriented and supportive
- excellent youth program
- bible school great!
- adult programs useful
- staff engages with worshippers but you don’t get pressured! This is a BIG plus. No pressure. Just relax and be there for the good words.
- volunteers and staff happy and healthy
I can go on and on with compliments.
Mesa Church is the best local small church in OC! Whether you're new to the faith or you've been walking with Jesus for a long time, this church is one of the best you'll find out there. This is my home away from home, for sure. How do you feel at home in mere moments? How do so many gather in 1 place that seem like they are a family? There is such honest to goodness Love in here. And the many generations of people who come here and have been here for years are wonderful.  It's precious and alive and true. From the  little ones, teens, young families, and seniors, they are all so inviting.
The pastor and his wife have such hearts for the Lord and for all these people here. And it is evident  they are truly adored back.  God is in the midst.
I'm Home.  If you need one, I highly recommend giving them a try...
you won't regret it.
They say here,  " There's always room at the table." And there is. Thankyou.. I'm pulling up a chair. ❤️ My 7 year old son loves this community. He has made friends here from attending Sunday mornings and Tuesday nights at the "Royal Rangers" program. He is able to retell Bible stories accurately, which I believe is credited to his time here. I even overheard him telling his friend that Jesus died on the cross for his sins during a car drive the other day as well. *****
There are no "fake OC" vibes here. Nothing but faithful people serving a faithful God. That might sound boring, but it's truly refreshing considering the location and time in which we live. ******

I have been able to join a small group at this church for a few years now. I have made friends through the group that have supported me during one of my most difficult seasons. ******

What I like most about this church is that you don't get lost in the crowd. People know that you are there and they genuinely want to know who you are as a person. They value input, and appreciate all volunteers on a consistent basis. ******

I LOVE that it's a multi generational church where you are able to glean love and wisdom from the older generations while learning from and cherishing the younger generations. *****

Mesa Church believes that "there is always room at the table." They make room for people from all walks of life. I believe that statement is true since I have experienced it first hand. I would encourage anyone looking for a place to belong, to come and experience it for themselves.

There are no "fake OC" vibes here. Nothing but faithful people serving a faithful God. That might sound boring, but it's truly refreshing considering the location and time in which we live. ******

I have been able to join a small group at this church for a few years now. I have made friends through the group that have supported me during one of my most difficult seasons. ******

What I like most about this church is that you don't get lost in the crowd. People know that you are there and they genuinely want to know who you are as a person. They value input, and appreciate all volunteers on a consistent basis. ******

I LOVE that it's a multi generational church where you are able to glean love and wisdom from the older generations while learning from and cherishing the younger generations. *****

Mesa Church believes that "there is always room at the table." They make room for people from all walks of life. I believe that statement is true since I have experienced it first hand. I would encourage anyone looking for a place to belong, to come and experience it for themselves.

name: Mesa Church Office
Mesa Church Office - Costa Mesa Campus
reviewSummary:
"There is always room at the table" at Mesa Church. I have been attending Mesa for the last year with my family. It has been a great experience. The pastoral staff is kind, personable, and intentional. Pastor Pete, Jordan, and Matt really care a lot about the people in their congregation. In has been awesome being apart of this community! We have been attending for about 11/2 years.  From day one we felt welcomed and at home.  The church has many opportunities to connect with the church body.  Growth track happens every Sunday and has 4 components:  What it means to have a personal relation with Jesus Christ,
; What the church is about; What are your personal gifts; What are the ways you may apply/serve using your gifts. I call this place the place where I can feel God in everything. Best community Church ever. reviewSummary: People there are very friendly. It is a service oriented church. Everyone is very kind and friendly and for a group of older people, they can be quite forward thinking. reviewSummary:
It is a Saturday. It's a long story but my wife was taken to Pomorado emergency from a rehab facility across the street for chest pains, she was supposed to be discharged today and I had to fight for them to help her. name: Metropolitan Community Church
Metropolitan Community Church - Pacific Beach Campus
reviewSummary:
For over a decade, The Met Church has been my spiritual home. Founded 54 years ago to serve the LGBTQ+ community, it remains a place of true inclusivity and acceptance. MCCSD goes beyond being open and affirming by remaining true to its roots. I have great pride to be an active part of such a strong community.

The sermons are a big part of what keeps me coming back. They're practical guidance I apply to my own life. The recent series on "The Four Agreements" was particularly impactful.

But The Met Church is more than great sermons. It's a vibrant community. Arriving early allows me to connect with friends, both new and old, and even strike up conversations with visitors.

The church also fosters a sense of community after the service. Hospitality always lays out a surprisingly tasty spread of coffee and snacks, providing a casual space to chat and get to know others. I usually stick around for about 10 minutes, enjoying the company and making new connections. It's a friendly place!

What truly resonates with me is The Met Church's approach to scripture. They take the Bible seriously, but not literally. This allows for open and honest discussions about faith, making it a welcoming space for people of all backgrounds and beliefs.

The attached pic is from our 2023 Church Planning Retreat. I have been attending Metropolitan Community Church in San Diego for over one year. I moved here from San Francisco (where I lived for 25+ years) and hoped to find a loving church community. Throughout my adult life, I have visited many churches but never really found anything that felt like a good fit. The moment I entered my first service at the Met, I immediately felt welcomed. Everyone is friendly, inviting, and non-pushy. The church's philosophy is "come as you are." You don't have to hold any specific religious beliefs. The outlook is that everyone is on their own spiritual journey. It's a very accepting church. Anyone that wants to may take communion. This gentle, loving approach is what draws me to the Met, and the people are truly loving, kind, and supportive. There is no pressure to believe or do anything. Another major upside is that the church is financially stable (for example, it owns its own building), so there is also no pressure to  contribute generously. I am confident you will find that this church will warmly welcome you and provide you the space, support and loving respect to nurture your deeply personal relationship with God, whatever it is meant to be for you. I am reflecting this morning on the blessing that is my home church, The Met.  I first found The Met online and was quickly drawn in by the weekly messages and the music.  I started attending in person a little over a year ago and leave service every Sunday feeling renewed and uplifted.  The last 3 months I had to go to Florida to help my sick parents so was grateful for the online ministry which allowed me to stay connected.  The services spoke to my heart from over 3000 miles away and sustained me during a difficult time.  I loved the opportunity to share the music and service with my mom and introduce her to the church I love.  Members of the church checked in with me regularly the entire time I was away.  If you are looking for an inclusive church that will meet you wherever you are in your spiritual journey, The Met is for you.  The people are fun loving, deeply committed to service and wonderfully diverse.  I was back in person this week and the welcome home touched my soul.  I thank God every day for this church. God guided me to the Metropolitan Community Church through their booth at the San Diego Pride Festival, and for that, I am deeply grateful. As a gay Christian, I spent many years feeling like an orphan, searching for a place of worship where I could praise God as my authentic self. From the moment I attended a service, I felt I had found that place. I experienced the love and presence of God in a way that resonated deeply with me. After two months of worship and connection, I joyfully decided to become a member and be baptized. Here, I can worship God fully, just as He created me, surrounded by love and acceptance. This Church is a place where you can be your authentic self.
From the very first day I stepped into MCCSD the presence of God was felt.
Now over 20 years later that feeling is still felt... especially on one unforgettable Sunday shortly after I was diagnosed with Stage 4 Lung Cancer. The physical presence of God touched my body; there was a warming sensation felt throughout. The message I received during this time was that I was not alone and everything would be OK.
Now almost 2 years later the cancer activity is undetectable through the treatment from my oncologist, the healing power of prayer from the Care Teams at MCCSD and the power of God.
I have a bright future ahead of my...Praise the Lord.

name: Mission 316 Church
Mission 316 Church - San Marcos Campus
reviewSummary:
A warm and wonderful church to worship, learn, grow and share life.  Get involved with the small groups and connect with caring, loving people.  Christ's love truly shines through the pastors, leaders and all the members.  Good, deep biblical teachings from warm, transparent pastors with good worship.  You won't regret visiting. From the moment I first walked into Mission316 church (about a year ago), I felt the presence of the Holy Spirit.  This is a loving, listening, sharing, body of people.  This is a Bible-based church that doesn't have a bunch of manmade rules.  If you want to hear and understand about our Heavenly Father and His Son in a casual and loving setting, I encourage you to give our church a try.  If you can't attend, the services are online.  Either way, I know your heart will be touched as God speaks to you through our wonderful pastors and musicians.  Be prepared to smile at the joy you'll feel! I love this church because 1) It's Bible based; very important to me. I don't want assumptions or different "takes" on my theology. I want the real deal. No prosperity gospel for me! 2) Our pastor, Alan Riggs makes the Bible come alive for me, with in-depth information about the text, language, and customs of the biblical times. 3) We are a small community church and everybody knows everybody else. We genuinely care about each other, and we are all growing in Christ, and we're also growing in each other's lives. Mission 3:16 IS my church. Been attending for well over 3 years, and look forward to every Sunday. BTW, before my daughter asked me to go with her one Sunday, I wasn't even going to church. I believed, but I had a bad taste in my spirit from trying out some of the mega churches with the "perfect" buildings & the professional band, etc. They struck me as sophisticated productions - and they were - but I get spiritually fed at Mission 3:16, and I'm just getting started! You won't know if you don't give it a try, so come on in on any Sunday, we'd love to meet you! Mission 3:16 is my home away from home.  Its full of love, great worship music, and loving people ready to welcome anyone that walks thru our doors, plus a loving pastor that preaches from the heart and the word of God. We also have a great children's ministry.
Come give us a try. You won't be disappointed. I love this church because the first time I came with my family, they welcome us with open arms it felt like a family gathering. Its been 7 years since that day, I'll never regret being welcome threw those door!

name: Mission Basilica San Juan Capistrano
Mission Basilica San Juan Capistrano - San Juan Capistrano Campus
reviewSummary: Fantastic place for a wedding. Rich history. I sing in the choir so a little bit biased. It's a wonderful church that I highly recommend. We have an 11:00 am mass w choir and a 1:00 pm Spanish mass w choir for the Spanish speaking people. Come join us! Beautiful church with great art and architecture. A great place to pray or simply relax. Note: This is NOT the original mission built in 1776. For that you have to walk down the block and pay the admission fee. The basilica church is free to enter and is an active parish. We had such a delightful day at Mission Basilica San Juan Capistrano! Mission Basilica San Juan Capistrano, located at 31520 Camino Capistrano in San Juan Capistrano, California, is a remarkable testament to historical architecture and spiritual significance. Completed in 1986, the basilica was thoughtfully designed to mirror the original 1806 Great Stone Church, which suffered destruction in the 1812 earthquake. This modern reconstruction serves as a vibrant parish, offering regular Mass services and housing a parochial school. Its designation as a minor basilica in 2000 and a national shrine in 2003 underscores its importance as a pilgrimage site and a center for community worship. Visitors and parishioners alike are drawn to its serene ambiance, rich history, and the active role it plays in fostering faith and education within the community.

name: Mission Bible Church
Mission Bible Church - Costa Mesa Campus
reviewSummary:
This is long overdue! Mission Bible Church has been instrumental in my walk as a Christian. The Lord led me here as a new believer, hungry for the Word in 2020.

Pastor Tony, a graduate of The Master's Seminary where he studied under John MacArthur, faithfully teaches the Bible through expository, verse-by-verse preaching. The Bible truly reigns supreme here.

The worship music is rich in truth--before you even hear the sermon, you are already singing biblical truth and offering praise to our Holy God.

Church membership at MBC allows you to be more than an attendee; you become part of the church body. Membership provides:
a) Accountability, which is a pathway to holiness, and
b) The opportunity to serve the Lord by serving His church, using the gifts He has given you.

Discipleship groups offer a place to meet weekly and grow alongside a small group of believers. As Pastor Tony says, "Hard preaching softens hearts," and sitting under the faithful preaching of God's Word will deepen your love for God and for others.

MBC also offers a variety of classes to support your spiritual growth, including Fundamentals of the Faith, Family Foundations (parenting), Evangelism & Apologetics, and the Builders Class (equipping for discipleship).

If you are looking to grow in your spiritual walk, be fed by God's Word, be equipped to live as an effective Christian, and be led faithfully--this is the church for you! , Romans 12:2 is a call to spiritual maturity, urging believers to intentionally cultivate a mindset that is aligned with God's truth and purpose, rather than being shaped by the transient and often harmful patterns of the world. Great Bible Non Denominational Church. 2 Suunday Services 9:00 am & 11:00 am 11 am service today was life changing. Thank you all so much. It hit hard. My husband and I have been attending this church for nearly 10 years. The love and faithfulness of the pastors and lay leaders is palpable. If you are looking for sound doctrine, verse by verse teaching, the gospel without gimmicks, and to be surrounded by a church family striving to be like Christ, this is the place you’ve been looking for.

name: Mission Hills Church - Aliso Viejo Campus
reviewSummary: Love my church and eternally grateful that God led me here 8+ years ago. God’s love and spirit is palpable from the moment you pull in to the lot. Every staff member I have met has exuded genuine care and kindness consistently. Highly recommend for anyone looking for a “home” church that focuses on scripture and Jesus’s life. My wife and I came to visit this church about six or seven months ago. We’ve lived in the area for over 20 years and have passed by this church many times. The first time we went people greeted us and were so friendly. The worship team is amazing and Pastor Bryan is an amazing teacher and humble man. We have made it our home church and feel part of the community. Our children and grandchildren visit and they love it too. They have something for everybody here from small groups to Programs assisting the community with A food pantry and a recovery program. I can’t say enough about Mission Hills Church Other than if you’re looking for a place to learn the Bible and feel the love of God this is it Hmnn, Hmnn. Brand new worship center. Pastor Bryan you do a great job and Pastor Karen, you make coming to Church a longing of the heart. . I have been here a couple of times. The worship sessions are always anointed and extravagant. The congregants are warm,  like everyone wants to love you and help you be a Great Christian! And the WORD? It comes from the throne of Grace seasoned with salt. marinated in mercy and served with grace! People, don't just take my word for it, even though you're busy, you should JUST COME. And you know what? There are two services every Sunday so you don't miss out by any means. So by all means, be there and come meet Jesus the King Exalted and Celebrated in His Body at the Mission Hills Church. I would gave given a 5-star rating, but Mission Hills Church is peopled by human beings still under construction, and still being molded by the Master Potter. I love.\nThis church , they make you feel like you're one of theirs , and they make you feel like family , that's why I continue to go back Truly authentic pastor and leadership team. This church demonstrates the heart of God every day with strong worship, tons of outreach both locally and globally and always looking for ways to do more. Moved out of the area a year ago, and we still drive over an hour every few months to attend.

name: Mission Hills Church - San Marcos Campus
reviewSummary:
If you are looking for a place to worship come  to Mission Hills Church and experience the warmth and love of Jesus.  You will be welcomed with open arms regardless of your story or walk of life. Great church if you like medium-sized church atmosphere. Lots of friendly people and the congregation tries to get to know everyone. Lots of bible-study groups for all ages on different days. I personally enjoy the young adults group (age 19 - 29) Bible studies and church travel retreats. I have been a part of Mission Hills Church since I was in middle school. I truly know this place as a second home and the members as church family. I have been a child, student, graduate, young adult, intern, and employee here, and my experience just keeps getting better and my faith gets stronger and deeper. This church and its pastors are genuine, accessible, wise, and kind. They truly care about care. Going there to visit back in December 2022 as a person of color I have never felt so singled out and Discriminated. I felt completely ignored and Totally shunned for not being white. Avoid this racist "church" at all costs if you're a person of color ! I hesitated to write a "review" for Mission Hills because it's not just a business to me—it's deeply personal, like family. But I want to share my experience because if you're searching for something meaningful, I think you should visit.

Spirituality has always been important in my life. Raised in a Catholic family that valued a personal connection with God and exploring different churches, I found Mission Hills Church after years of seeking. What stood out to me was their sincere commitment to teaching from the Bible—it's genuine and firmly rooted in scripture. The staff's friendliness, warmth, and nonjudgmental attitude also made a significant impression on me.

Mission Hills goes beyond mere entertainment; it provides a peaceful environment focused on meaningful teaching that deepens your relationship with God. The children's ministry, in particular, has been enriching for my family. Overall, Mission Hills has given me a fresh perspective, prioritizing substance over superficiality. I'm grateful for the peace and insight I've gained there.

name: Mission Road Church
Mission Road Church - Tallahassee Campus
reviewSummary:

The worship is really fun (My dad plays guitar on the worship team). And they have a babies room, a preschool-kindergarten room (at least I’m pretty sure that it’s preschool-kindergarten), and an elementary room for the kids to go in during service. We get to pray, play games, hang with our homies, worship, listen to a sermon, it’s just so great. I love my church. I love praising God, especially when I’m at Mission Road Church. Peace and Love, y’all! ✝︎❤️
“The Lord is my shepherd, I lack nothing. He makes me lie down in green pastures, he leads me beside quiet waters, he refreshes my soul. He guides me along the right paths for his name’s sake. Even though I walk through the darkest valley, I will fear no evil, for you are with me; your rod and your staff, they comfort me. You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies. You anoint my head with oil; my cup overflows. Surely your goodness and love will follow me all the days of my life, and I will dwell in the house of the Lord forever.”-Psalms 23 i was made to feel special and welcome! such a laid back hip place to celebrate Jesus’ salvation! honestly i haven’t been to church in years besides tv church. very moving music! and the sermon was very motivational! i highly recommend anyone check out Genesis Church! There is no judgement, clothing, whatever! i didn’t run into a single negative vibe! the entire church was a overflow of positivity!  amazing! i feel charged up! ready to celebrate Easter! They have a ton of events please look into it! Love this Church and Pastor Scott! The church has changed quite a bit from when I first attended. At the beginning of service, the sing to praise the Lord. It used to be 3 songs and now it is four songs which reduces the time that  Pastor Scott preaches the word! I would rather here the word than a 30 minute gospel concert.
All chorus people on stage used to sing altogether. Now , they do not leaving only Pastor Stephanie to do the lead singing! We are praising the Lord and everyone should be singing not just Pastor Stephanie! I do love this church and love going to it! I just wish they would go back to the 3 songs and preach the word longer. Such a wonderful place to call home. I have became a member in October of 2017 and have loved it ever since. The first day I attended Genesis Church was when a hurricane knocked out most power in town. I was looking for a church to go to and the one I originally planned on going to was closed. Genesis had no power in its main building, but some how there was power in the small one. The service was so touching and the atmosphere was very welcoming. I felt comfortable there. Pastor Scott and his team do a great job of being available and making sure that everyone who comes into Genesis is talked to by someone. Genesis Church also does a lot of local events, trying to help our community. I appreciate the compassion there is at Genesis. Genesis Church is amazing! I'm beyond grateful to have found this church a few years ago! Being around people and a pastor who are so passionate about God's love and the importance of showing His love in our daily lives, has given me the support and inspiration to continually grow in my faith and relationship with God. I also enjoy working with the young children in Genesis Kids, connecting with the families and giving back is so rewarding!

name: Mission San Juan Capistrano
Mission San Juan Capistrano - San Juan Capistrano Campus
reviewSummary:
A visit to Mission San Juan Capistrano is truly special. The mission is incredibly well preserved, with so many fascinating artifacts and relics to explore—it really brings history to life.

The grounds are absolutely stunning. There are vibrant blooms everywhere, from succulents to rose bushes, creating a peaceful and colorful atmosphere. It also attracts a lot of wildlife, which adds to the charm and makes the experience feel even more serene.

They have a lovely little gift shop and even a vegetable garden, which adds a nice touch to the visit. This is a perfect spot for special occasion photography or even a meaningful school field trip. The Experience & History:
This is a perfect stop on the way to Laguna Beach.
​Historical Significance: This is a stunning historical building that has been around since 1776 (currently celebrating 250 years).
​Atmosphere: The mission buildings are historic and very well maintained. It is a very calm, family-friendly area that is great for walking around and taking photos.
​Tours: A great touch is that they provide a self-guide program in several languages, making the history very accessible to everyone.
​Logistics:
​Admission: I paid $18 per person, which is well worth it to explore and help preserve the grounds.
​Parking: Be aware that street parking is limited directly in front, but it is easily walkable to public parking lots nearby.
​Verdict:
A beautifully preserved piece of California history. I definitely recommend stopping by! Excellently preserved historical site, and very educational. I didnt partake in the audio tour option, but the fact that it was there, along with the many stations to use it on, show that it is used well. Got to see some students on site - glad to see the child education still goes strong, even after my personal elementary education visited here decades ago.

Somewhat related, the gift store on site could use more history books related to the mission, and the colonization period. Not a miss, for sure, but would have been a bonus for history enthusiasts such as myself. The historical place is a must visit. It was beautiful. They will give you some kind of remote control to listen the history of the people and places. The only thing we did not like is that they did not let us take pictures of my husband and I. The staff lady said it’s not allowed to take pictures with props and tripod. Otherwise we have to pay $200 dollars. We were just wearing white casual dress and long sleeves polo with my husband with his khaki pants and it was tucked out. It was a casual wear and it didn’t allow us to take pictures. We are not professional photographers. It was our first  time to visit. We were disappointed of not having taking pictures by ourselves. We didn’t have anybody else to take our pictures so we had to bring a phone stand. But it wasn’t allowed. We don’t want to bother asking anyone to take our picture. I thought it was the best place to take pictures of us for our anniversary. I just thought it would be memorable for us. The staff lady didn’t let us. So disappointing. Very beautiful Mission. They have free audio tour devices that went into much details. Staff was friendly. Price of admission is worth it with how much there was to see. I went at 2pm and closed at 5pm and within those 3 hours I still didn't see everything (I was listening to the audio guide so I took my time learning the history of the mission). Children might not appreciate all the historical information but its still beautiful to walk around and keep them engaged. The church inside the mission is beautiful. Heads up, weddings are not allowed but I did see 5 couples bring a photographer and in weddings attire, don't know if you have to ask permission for that.

name: Mission San Luis Rey
Mission San Luis Rey - Oceanside Campus
reviewSummary:
After exploring the main mission church, you can enter the museum right through the gift shop for an adult admission fee of $8. This seems to be the standard setup for most California Old Missions, making it very easy to find. I’ve visited about 5 to 6 missions so far, but this was only my third time checking out the actual museum, and I am so glad I did. 🏛️📜

The museum does a wonderful job explaining the history and conditions of the early missionary era. It feels very much like an anthropology and history museum, packed with rich historical evidence and fascinating artifacts. Walking through the exhibits and seeing the deep historical roots also gave me a beautiful moment of reflection on how my own faith has evolved over time, which left me feeling incredibly proud and fulfilled. 🙏✨

It takes about 30 minutes to thoroughly look through everything, making it a perfect, quick addition to your visit. If you want to dive deeper into the rich history behind the mission, I highly recommend stopping by! ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ I didn’t know what to expect going in, but it was absolutely beautiful. The architecture and the rich history of the mission made it a truly memorable experience. The staff were incredibly kind and helpful throughout my visit. I would highly recommend this place to anyone considering a pilgrimage. Very well maintained mission - free to enter, but with an entry fee for museum.  We enjoyed the chapel, met a friendly Franciscan brother, and lingered in the peaceful courtyard cafe over cold brew coffee.  Small gift shop. Its beautiful 🥰🙏🙏 I bought holy water and some saint charms. I saw a man praying the rosary outside & it broke my heart. Wish I would've asked him if he was ok....Still thinking about the situation.  Will pray for him We had a delightful evening at the Candlelight Concert at San Luis Rey Mission. The concert was professionally organized and the technology very convenient.
The staff were friendly and diligent, and the concert as promised. Beautiful setting and the musicians, young as they were, also very accomplished. We’ll gladly repeat the experience.

name: Mount Soledad Presbyterian Church
Mount Soledad Presbyterian Church - La Jolla Campus
reviewSummary:
I’ve been a part of this church for nine years. I love it. It is my second family I feel welcomed as my authentic self every time I come. The Worship is amazing beyond words on Sundays and the sermons are relatable and introspective.  The small groups and events are meaningful and fun and creative.
This place is not over the top, nor preachy,  nor judgey. It’s just a group of welcoming people who aim to love their neighbors, become better versions of themselves, and grow in their faith with God. If you are curious, stop in.   If you want to screen an online sermon before you come, give Easter April 5 2026 a listen. What a committed membership for this congregation led church. Whether through music, prayer or sermons, the worship ministry fosters a spirit of inclusion. Many opportunities to grow in faith through a variety of ministries. My granddaughter and grandson always look forward to church and the children and youth programs. This has been such a wonderful place for our family. The worship is contemporary with occasional hymns mixed in and is SO good. Every message from Pastor Markus is put in context, and even when the passage is something I've heard preached on before, I come away with a new perspective on it and a way to apply it to my life. Our kids love Sunday school where they quickly came to know all of the kids. They are sad when the Thursday night bible study is on break because they can't wait to go play with their friends (and hear a Bible story from the ministry director :)).

The best part of this church is the welcoming congregation. After a few weeks of attending it felt like we were already a part of the church. There are people of all ages and we all love to fellowship with delicious snacks after service. When we began our church hunt in San Diego, we thought it was going to be a long string of months until we found our home -- but after visiting Mount Soledad one time, we immediately fell in love. Pastor Markus is knowledgeable, funny, and open-minded. Plus, he puts scripture into its proper historical context -- you'll learn an occasional Greek word, see an occasional map, and learn what was really going on in every passage. I feel like I learn something new every sermon.

Most importantly to us, this church feels like a real community -- people get to know each other, there is a small group and prayer group every week, and the Sunday school is small and unintimidating for our kids. (They LOVE it there. Where once our kids felt ho-hum about going to church, now they beg to go every Sunday -- if that doesn't sell you on Mount Soledad, I don't know what will!) Mount Soledad Presbyterian Church is a warm welcoming place of worship. My husband and I have been attending for years and absolutely love everything about it. The worship is amazing, I look forward to it every Sunday. Pastor John is a strong leader, he is very present and always makes time for our family. The sermons are relatable and really speak to your heart. The congregation is friendly and it makes you feel at home. Our two children thrive in the Sunday school program. I love how they leave so excited to tell us about what they leaned about the Bible that Sunday. Our family invites anyone looking for a church to call home to visit Mount Soledad Presbyterian Church. It is a wonderful church.
