reviewSummary:
Wonderful place to worship. I attended Mass at 11:30am in Sunday and it was packed. I love the English hymns with the Roman Liturgy. The parish members are welcoming. I’d like to take my family again when we visit Irvine. Mass is done here in the Anglican Use of the Roman Rite. Despite being in the Diocese of Orange, it falls under the jurisdiction of the Ordinariate of the Chair of St. Peter. Very small location, but its Mass is much more reverent than those found in larger Catholic Churches. Father Glenn is a very good homilist and defends the honor of the liturgy, and the music is very conducive to proper worship. Deacon Christopher was only ordained a year ago. Very personable church. Small and close-knit congregation. Part of the Ordinariate of the Catholic Church. Anglicans and Episcopalians thinking of converting to Catholicism would feel very at home here. I would probably feel like I needed confession if I rated a Catholic Church less than five stars; the primary purpose of this review is to highlight some things that I know people care about when looking for a Mass or a parish.

- This church is part of the Ordinariate of the Chair of St. Peter, not the Diocese of Orange. The Ordinariate was set up for Anglican converts, and answers directly to the Pope. It is a legit Catholic Church authorized to use an Anglican-style liturgy. The priest is an Anglican convert.

- The priest here faces the altar during the Mass and communion is received kneeling and on the tongue. The Mass is not in Latin, but parts of it are different if you are used to a regular Roman mass.

- This church is inside a larger building, a law firm that has a Catholic chapel attached. This sounds weird, but it is very nice inside. St JHN is a wonderful, small Catholic Church.  Seating is very limited, but the setting is intimate.  No microphones needed.  The singing was very solemn and respectful.  I attended during a Prinicipal Mass which covered a lot of ritual and liturgy.  The homily was tremendously mature and informative.  I wish my own church offered the depth of spiritual understanding and instruction.  Great Sunday!

Listening to the mighty pipe organ in the beautiful church sanctuary is one of the most moving and amazing experiences to be had in Jacksonville! Thank you for opening your church to the larger community for these much appreciated, deeply enjoyed and memorable performances! My husband and I have been members of the choir at St. John's Cathedral since 1981. My husband and I love the music program there. Both our former choirmaster/organist, John Barry, and our current one, Tim Tuller, are amazing musicians. It has been and is a privilege to work with both of them. We love the Anglican style choral music. I love to play my cello in the services from time to time. Our choir has made two pilgrimages to England, singing services at Ely Cathedral, Westminster Cathedral and Canterbury Cathedral. We also went on a pilgrimage trip to Washington DC where we were in residence at the National Cathedral. The congregation at St. John's contains some of the nicest people around and we always welcome newcomers. Hope you'll visit. Warm & inviting. Although I'm Baptist by birth, I couldn't have felt more welcomed.  The minister, Rev. Mark Anderson, delivered a very encouraging & worthy message that inspires hope!

Rev. Anderson shared an unforgettable story about two particular groups who were stranded out in the Arctic.  One resorted to crude means of survival & only 3 survived.

However, the other group cleverly appointed tasks based on ingenuity of the individuals, even assigning a minister.  This bonding teamwork provided a better outcome of survival for the two groups.

reviewSummary:
My review will be a little long. It comes with love/ heart, honesty, and faith. Born catholic; would attend mass Sundays and a few events here and there.. not very involved. My love for Jesus started 4 years ago. Living testimony of Gods love and mercy: that’s another story. My miracle made me search for events in different churches. Did not want to commit to any. I will attend anything from worship nights, Holy Spirit nights, special healing masses, monthly priest talks, adoration, prayer, book readings, etc. In search of spiritual, emotional and physical healing and strength. That strength that Jesus gives me to overcome any life challenges and obstacles aimed my way was my miracle motivation and promise to attend 1 hour mass or pray.

One night Jesus had a plan for me; You can say a life lesson or purpose. I ended in an event hosted by St. Joseph Catholic Church. 3 days of that event and then after the event a light fellowship for the community. I purchased the guest book. Church volunteers were very welcoming and that’s where Jesus made his way. I attended a few group meetings. After meeting Father Martin, a few of his talks, blessings, masses, guidance/ confessions, good listener, caring and support for all his community. I chose to leave the fear behind and decided my commitment to Jesus would be to serve in St. Joseph.

A blessing open the door for me to volunteer in Faith formation- Awesome leader thank you Michelle,  that lead to English Hospitality/ Sunshine greeters, then Alpha Course, Catholic 101, Bible class, Women Retreats, Adoration, Rosary, etc. Thank you all can’t name all. I would have to make my review even longer.

I can only say thank you Jesus for that night.  Jesus guided me to a community that has taught me a lot. Welcomed me, made me part of the community family and I feel at home. One year now almost two. This church values are focused In building personal relationships, working as a team/ unity and no division in groups, all church coming together to help serve others with passion and grace.

The Holy Spirit is felt in St. Joseph church. Jesus presence all around. I can keep going.This review is based on my personal experience’s. I Invite you to gods calling and join us at St. Joseph mass or events and open your heart to your own personal encounter with Jesus.

God bless all,

Ms. Teresita Thank you for an amazing Appreciation Dinner. The food was fabulous. I appreciate feeling so welcome and am very proud of this amazing parish. Great job rocking the party Fr Martin Literally one of the best spiritual places I could ever hope for - and it's fun here! I get so spiritually enriched through attending daily mass (8:30am), weekend mass + events, and my involvement in Women's Ministry (we have a great Women's Bible Study here on Thursdays!) I encourage people to stay involved here - it's very worthwhile. For being a small church, we have a lot going here! Come join us ⚜️ Such a warm and loving community! From the moment we walked through the doors, we were greeted with friendly smiles and made to feel right at home. The members are incredibly genuine, and it's the perfect place to grow both spiritually and relationally. Highly recommend this church! The worship is uplifting, and the pastor's messages are practical, encouraging, and easy to apply to everyday life. It has an authentic, relaxed atmosphere, and the children's program is fantastic—my kids are always excited to go back. I made my First Holy Communion here at Saint Joseph’s Placentia in March 1987 and my baptism on Easter 1981! Everyone is so kind and wonderful! Thanks 🙏 everyone at Saint Joseph’s my family and Godparents! Thommas & Lorraine Clements, Carmen Grey and Fredrick Hirn!

name: St. Joseph Catholic Church - Los Angeles (Downtown) Campus
reviewSummary:
I was asked to leave my own brother’s funeral service at church because my son, who has autism, was making noise. Being removed during such a painful moment made an already heartbreaking day even more difficult.
A so called priest asked us to leave.

Autism awareness matters everywhere, including in churches.

!
* Mark 10:14–16: Jesus became indignant when disciples turned children away, stating the kingdom belongs to them, then embraced and blessed them. Bells ringing eight times every weekend morning at odd hours is not tradition, it’s a nuisance to every neighbor within earshot. A little self-awareness goes a long way. It's absolutely not appropriate to remove a child from a church service simply for being noisy. We are often encouraged to help out in our congregation, but what are we supposed to do with our little ones in those moments? The church itself is very beautiful and the priest Rafael is amazing. He is speaks clearly also for the kids to understand the mass, he gives them examples. And what can I say he has everybody attentive during the mass due to his knowledge and he helping us get closer to god. Padre Rafael also goes for the Chivas de Guadalajara!  😊 Beautiful church, their Sunday mass has mariachis for music! Really fantastic! Also, father Rafael is a hoot. Gives great sermons and has a great sense of humor.

reviewSummary:
Let me start by saying this review is not about the church itself but specifically about the school and its staff.

My son started attending St. Joseph Preschool at the beginning of January. The first week went well but by the second week I started receiving complaints that he was “too active” and didn’t listen. Five weeks later the director Suzy asked me to reduce his schedule from five days to three because the teachers were unable to do the bare minimum and manage him. I declined due to my work as I occasionally help my husband and was also preparing to start a new job. The very next day they began sending me videos of my son running around while his teacher, Ms. Rita sat and did nothing and the TA Lindsey recorded him instead of redirecting him. I responded respectfully saying I would talk to my son but reducing his days was not an option.
Right after I sent that message she replied back saying that he was “not a good fit” and given two weeks for reevaluation. I was even told I should inform my new job “never mind” in case he couldn’t remain at the school. When I met with Suzy in person and asked what I could do to help she was not willing to work with me. When I asked what would happen if he improved during those two weeks (which he did) she sarcastically laughed in my face and said “maybe in the miracle of St. Joseph” instead of giving me some hope. During those 2 weeks 3 different teachers worked with my son and all of them told me he was doing well, listening, and behaving well. They did mention that he is active but also said that this is normal for kids his age and have kids who act worse than him in that school and specifically
in that class. These teachers were kind, professional, and clearly cared about the children. (You know who you are) I later found out from staff that Lindsey the TA  had been taking unnecessary pictures of my son and sending them to Suzy claiming he wasn’t cooperating even on days he was doing well. One teacher even confronted her about how unnecessary that was after it happened in front of her. What’s most frustrating is that the school refused to make any accommodations for my son, yet made adjustments for another child within just one week, even moving that child to a different class. Suzy and Roseann were extremely rude throughout this entire process. I reached out to Roseann and never received a response. On his last day she told me that he’s really not a good fit and was speaking to me with such a bad attitude as if I or my son did something bad to her. She also told me if I provided a doctor’s note explaining how to “handle” my son, they might consider taking him back. despite the fact that he is completely normal and simply active. They offended me in so many way on so many levels but I kept it calm just for my son to stay.  On his last day after they gave me all his stuff I also noticed that his pull-ups were barely used which shows that he wasn’t being properly changed throughout the day. It became very clear that this school is inconsistent and very very unprofessional. These people are in for the money. If you donate money for them they will take care of your child. It’s all about hookups!! There seems to be favoritism, and not all children are treated equally. After this happened I found out that a few parents have argued with Suzy and left because of her nasty attitude. My son was essentially removed for behaving like a typical 3 year old. Now my son is attending another school where he is thriving and receiving ZERO complaints. Sending my son to St. Joseph was the worst decision I made. I strongly recommend that parents reconsider enrolling their children here until major improvements are made in staff training, communication, and overall care. Otherwise, stay away from this place. This church new name is Saint Joseph Chaldean Catholic Church

8:30 AM - Chaldean

reviewSummary:
Beautiful church and outstanding mass celebration. The priest was very friendly and welcoming to us, as it was our first time attending mass here. They have mass in Syriac and English on Tuesdays & Thursdays, and it was so easy to follow along. They have the liturgy in a book where you could follow along word for word. Definitely want to re-visit this beautiful church. And they’re in communion with Rome 🙏🏻 Mass every every morning at 9:00, Saturday at 5:30 pm and Sunday at 11:00 am
They have a gorgeous banquet hall available for rent any day of the week for great prices!! Honestly, everything here just feels right, you can feel God’s presence. It is very beautiful. God bless! Wonderful Church and wonderful people :) Father Fadi and his beautiful ❤️ wife Nicole are very welcoming as well as all the community at this lovely Church. The mass here is mixed English and Lebanese/Arabic. Come over and introduce yourself, get to know the parishioners and enjoy some of the food they prepare and sell after mass, delicious.. The Church ladies also cater Lebanese Mediterranean food, And u can rent out the hall for your special occasions and events. See you soon in God's will at this beautiful Church of Jesus 🙏🙏😍 Wonderful new church with a very friendly congregation of mosty Lebanese, Syrian, Jordanian, Iraqi, and Egyptian families. Mass is Sundays at 11 and lasts for 1 hour, everyone is welcome to join and discover this beautifully diverse community.  They host an exciting Lebanese cultural festival every year with great music and dancing, delicious Mediterranean/Lebanese food, and all kinds of activities. It's nice to have a church like this in Riverside so we don't have to drive to Orange county or LA or San Diego to gather with other Christian Arabs

name: St. Joseph’s Cathedral
St. Joseph’s Cathedral - San Diego (Downtown) Campus
reviewSummary:
Very beautiful, very holy, and very faithful church!  The priest had a great homily!  The parish is very active!  Without doubt I strongly recommend going to Saint Joseph’s Cathedral!  Know our Savior Jesus loves you and have a great day!❤️✝️🙏⚓️🕊️⛪️😃 Be careful walking down the stairs off of 3rd Ave entrance.  They are steep and numerous for the elderly. If you're not familiar with this church, you'll have no other choice but to use them.  Please know that there is a flat entrance on the 4th Ave side with  wheelchair access as well.

This is a beautiful, enormous cathedral! How sad. Visiting the area and wanted to stop in the church. I had not been back in 25 years. I paid for parking walked up to the front doors and found them locked at 2 o’clock in the afternoon. A man painting out front said that the church was closed. No signage indicating church hours. So I called the office and the recording said that the church was open Tuesday through Friday from 9 AM to 5 PM. I spoke to someone named father Peter Navarro and explained the situation and he really didn’t seem to care. All he said was where did you find out the information about the church hours and when I told him that it was on the recording all he said was that’s fine to know. Nothing else. Not exactly a very welcoming message to the faithful. It was a very beautiful Catholic cathedral. There are many  life size statues of many wonderful saints. There is also a new statue of Mother Teresa sank teresa and the Pope John it is gorgeous cathedral lovely lit and the acoustics are wonderful. For a mass today we had the I don't know how many pipes are in the Oregon but it's a big organ up in the loft and there was singing at the mass it was very spiritual. It reminded me of masses when I was a child absolutely lovely. There is a restroom and free parking. I love to come to mass here. It has the traditional church feeling. It's a beautiful church.

reviewSummary:
I recently started attending St. Kieran, and I must say it is a wonderful place for prayer and reflection. The Mass is truly beautiful and conducted with great reverence, which creates a very peaceful and spiritual atmosphere.
The church itself is lovely and well-maintained. What I appreciate the most is the welcoming and serene environment—it's a perfect place for anyone looking for a quiet, holy space to connect with God. I highly recommend this parish to anyone in the El Cajon area looking for a meaningful and peaceful liturgical experience. My Family's church for many years, actually following the Word of God. Saint Kieran’s Catholic School is an amazing school. The principle Dr. Belcher and her staff are top notch. I highly recommend and commend their diligent effort towards the children’s progress from grades K- 8. This is a safe and caring environment where the kids are always number one! Beautiful service, nice church, great leadership in Father Ben and Deacon Frank.  That said, it is a clicky community and some people are treated like outsiders. We actually went for the open house for their school.  It was very nice, very clean and had some of the nicest people I have ever met.

reviewSummary:
This Sunday, I was blessed to worship at Saint Mark’s Episcopal Church in Glendale (1020 N. Brand Blvd, Glendale, CA 91202). The morning sunlight poured gently through the stained glass, painting the sanctuary in hues of gold and rose. The choir lifted their voices in a harmony that felt angelic, drawing every heart into the presence of the Holy.

There’s something profoundly sacred about Saint Mark’s — a sense that generations of prayer still linger in the walls, that faith has been spoken and sung here long before us. Saint Mark, the Evangelist, reminds us that the Gospel is not just a story to be read, but a calling to be lived — to proclaim hope, to serve with love, and to move with urgency toward what is good and true.

My prayer this Sunday is for clarity and courage — that the Holy One would reveal truth where confusion reigns, and light where shadows still linger. I pray for all who labor quietly for justice, for those who refuse to hate even when hated, and for every soul longing to be seen and loved as they are. Especially, I lift up the LGBTQ+ community — may Gods protection and peace surround them always, and may every heart learn to see Their divine image in one another. Great, Welcoming Entrance.

I am overjoyed to share that I have been baptized and officially welcomed into this incredible faith community! My heart is full of gratitude for the love, support, and guidance I’ve received throughout this deeply meaningful journey.

To the wonderful people who took the time to share the Word of God and guide me through the program, thank you for your wisdom and encouragement. Your teachings helped me grow in faith and feel prepared for this sacred moment.
A very special thank you to Father Joseph, our remarkable pastor. His warmth and genuine care make everyone feel at home. He has taken the time to know my family by name, and his welcoming spirit truly embodies the love of Christ. St. Matthew is blessed to have such a compassionate and inspiring leader.
I feel incredibly lucky to call myself part of the St. Matthew Church family. This community radiates God’s love, and I am so grateful to be embraced by such a caring and faithful group of people. May God continue to bless this church, its mission, and every heart within it.

With love and gratitude,

Sara Odiesh I don’t usually write reviews like this, but I felt it was important to share my experience—especially for other single parents or individuals trying to return to their faith.

I was raised Catholic. I’ve received my sacraments and have always planned to baptize my children when the time was right. Life hasn’t been easy. I’ve been a single mom since 2017, raising two boys on my own, pursuing higher education, and working hard to build a better life for my little family. Despite the challenges, I’ve always kept my faith close to my heart.

Last year, I visited this church. The same one where I received my First Communion and Confirmation. At first, a kind lady gave me information about the baptism process, and I felt welcomed. This March, I returned to get the forms again and confirm dates, but I was met with a very different experience.

The secretary, Rebecca, was cold, dismissive, and made me feel incredibly unwelcome. She questioned my faith, implying I wasn’t a true Catholic because I hadn’t been attending that particular church regularly. When I kindly asked for the dates, she responded by saying, “How can you call yourself Catholic and not go to church?”

What that secretary said to me was unfair, unkind, and entirely out of line with the compassion and grace that the Catholic Church should represent. I came in with sincerity, ready to do things right for my boys and for myself and instead of receiving support, I left feeling judged and disheartened.

Everyone’s journey is different. As a mother, a student, and someone who has walked a long and difficult path, I expected understanding, not shame. I’m sharing this because people deserve to know how they might be treated here, and I hope this encourages the church leadership to reflect on how their representatives speak to members of the community—especially those coming in with hope and faith in their hearts. Do not sign your kids up for catechism classes here. I signed up my youngest for her first communion and my oldest for her confirmation classes. The lady in charge of the program (Rachel) is condescending and are way too strict for classes taught by volunteers with no proper training or accreditation. Kids have to sign in every sunday for mass but it HAS to be the kid, you cannot sign in for them even with your kid standing right next to you and even if your kid does not know how to write. If you attend a different parish, you have to take pictures with the priest at the front of the church and send it in for credit. They cancel classes when things come up for them but you cannot call off because its counted against you. I understand doing classwork but there is no reason for homework (my opinion) and Rachel flat out called us liars because i said my daughter told me her teacher doesnt remind the class about assignments (mind you my daughter is an A-B student in advance classes so there is no reason for her to lie). They also let you waste your time attending classes even if your student will not be eligible to move to second year. I was hoping for a better experience like I had at my old Parish in Anaheim but unfortunately this was the first place I attended after moving to Corona and I would not recommended it. I will be moving over to St Edwards and hope to have a more pleasant experience. We had myselfs Momma and Dads funeral mass here as well as the Reception in the church hall.
It was a very beautiful service and Fr Joseph was did a wonderful job.
Someday I hope to attend a wedding there...bp Very poor team. Wanted to baptize my child with them. They've only been very difficult and argumentative during the whole process. Before we paid for anything we confirmed with the Baptism coordinator, Evelyn, multiple times that once we paid for the class we would be able lock in the date for the baptism. Only after we paid for the class and attended the class that they told us there was more that needed to be done and wouldn't assist us. And even told my wife to get new Godparents.
I don't understand why a church would want to turn away a child for Baptism. They also don't care about or believe in COVID and wouldn't work with us to try and accommodate the health and safety of ourselves, them, or my 3 month old baby. I used to attend this parish but I will never again attend and will highly recommend for people to go elsewhere.
They're fantastic at taking your money but fall very short at trying to help you in anyway that doesn't involve a transaction.

I would definitely attend Mass here again if in the area. Best Church in the valley.  Everything about this place is beautiful; the church, the choir, the liturgy.  This place feels like home and you can tell the presence of God is here.  Father Steve’s homilies are always touching and thoughtful. I look forward to coming here every Sunday! Do be advised that depending on what time you go you will get a different experience when it comes to music.  Saturday nights and Sunday at 8 and 9:30am don’t have a choir and will have more modern music.  The 11am mass has the traditional hymns and a choir.  If you’re like me and prefer the traditional music you will want to go at 11am. Either way though you will be blessed by coming here! They also have a daily afternoon mass at 5:30pm which most parishes do not have.

name: St. Monica Catholic Church
St. Monica Catholic Church - Santa Monica Campus
reviewSummary: A beautiful church building, I highly recommend visiting. If you are new to the Catholic faith (convert) this may be a good church to get into. They sing and clap during the Mass with a full band. The priest ad-libbed a few times during Mass. An example would be for the concluding prayer. He didn't say let us pray and no one stood up for it. The Eucharistic prayer was said correctly, but this is definitely not a conservative church community. Still, I believe the Mass was valid, the people participating were kind, and the church building was beautiful. I would visit again for a tour. I was very under prepared for how contemporary this church is in the music selection and practice. Be prepared for LA showtunes version of the service, very, very brief pauses and no bells calling down the holy spirit. I write this review because I wished I'd read Google beforehand so I was more prepared. When the Google summary description of this parish says "contemporary" it means it. I'll likely be finding a slightly more meditative Mass for myself while I'm in the area but if you're coming from a more contemporary practice and transitioning to Catholicism then might be a good exploration. Nice St. Monica Catholic Church. Nice people and very active group. Very big and spacious hall. Good for your next events. Inquire at the administration office for more details. So, I bake my mother's recipe for Pumpkin pies every Thanksgiving for my family I've been doing this for about 15 years now.  I always make the filling and fill the pie crust on the Tuesday night  before the holiday, so the pies are as fresh as possible and the filling flavor left overnight, really soaks into the crust making for  much more delicious pies. That said today, I called St Monica's my church to find out where to  donate the two  extra  pies that I made special for the Thanksgiving dinner for the needy tonight. Only to be told over the phone "Sorry you missed the deadline, which was on Monday". The lady was rude and abrupt with me, So I ended up giving the pies to the West Side Food Bank  in Santa Monica, which was more than happy to take the pies. I have to say If I was running a food drive especially given the economy today, with more people in need than in recent years. I'd make an exception. She was apparently too busy to ask someone if they would still be willing to take the pies.   So as of today I will no longer donate to St Mo's charity food drives.  And if they are short on pies  tonight, anyone is shorted on desert,  they can thank that rude woman on the phone that basically told me "What do you want me to do about it?  You missed the deadline". I don't know maybe it's just me. but when people are hungry I'll bend the rules to be sure they get to eat. Great three level underground parking. Beautiful church.

name: St. Patrick Catholic Church
St. Patrick Catholic Church - Miami Beach Campus
reviewSummary:
We visited St. Patrick Catholic Church in Miami Beach over the holiday weekend, and it was a beautiful experience. The church itself is absolutely beautiful, and we were blessed to participate in a very reverent and moving Mass.

I especially appreciated Father Russell. He was a wonderful priest to listen to, and the way he celebrated the Mass really stood out. He seemed to have everything memorized, but more than that, he prayed and spoke in a way that felt personal, almost as if he was saying the words directly to each parishioner. It made the Mass feel fresh and meaningful, almost like hearing it for the first time again.

Overall, it is a beautiful church with a beautiful Mass, and we were very grateful to have visited. Absolutely beautiful Catholic Church. The parking is easy to find across the street but when there’s a large event definitely go early. It becomes nearly impossible to find a space. Also avoid if it’s raining this area floods excessively. Mass is great and everyone is friendly here. There’s also dogs allowed in the rear of the church. A special atmosphere! The Monsignor gave a wonderful homily on the occasion I attended, as it was a confirmation ceremony for the students from the school affiliated with St. Patrick’s Church! I highly recommend checking the Mass schedule and attending services. Beautiful church,
Beautiful garden on the side.
Everyone was very welcoming San Patrick is one of the most beautiful churches in Miami and Miami Beach area. Not only in its architecture, but also in its celebrations, the music, the staff, everything.

The liturgy is always impeccable, and the choir and orchestra are one of the best I have heard. I really like going because you get to enter a very spiritual environment.

On days of big celebrations like Christmas and Easter, many people go to masses. It has ample parking and is very well located.

It also has a small store that sells religious items.

Without a doubt one of the best churches in the city to visit or attend mass.

name: St. Paul the Apostle Catholic Church
St. Paul the Apostle Catholic Church - Chino Hills Campus
reviewSummary:
We had a beautiful experience at St. Paul Apostle Church for my daughters’ baptism. From the beginning, the church staff was kind, organized, and very helpful in guiding us through the process. The baptism ceremony itself was meaningful, peaceful, and truly special for our family. The priest made us feel welcomed and took the time to explain the sacrament in a way that was easy to understand and very touching. We are grateful for such a memorable and faith-filled experience and are thankful to St. Paul Apostle Church for making this important day so special for our daughters. Highly recommend to families looking for a loving and respectful parish. So pretty!!! I love the architecture of the church and its so peaceful! Everyone is so polite and inviting. The pews are padded so you are comfortable sitting. I have lived nearby a couple years and I just decided to go visit for Ash Wednesday. To my surprise I felt like I was home and fell in love with the church. There is plenty of parking and it's easy to navigate through. On your way in or out, stop by the grotto area where Mary is. It's a beautiful private area for her. I will be making this my home church. Thank you for making me feel so welcome As a child, I admit I used to fall asleep in church -- but this is no ordinary church, let alone your ordinary Catholic church. Being new to the area and only here for a few months, I felt a bit apprehensive about attending a new parish.

From the moment I stepped into the sanctuary, I felt genuinely welcomed. Between Masses, I approached Father Uche Onyekwelu and, in need of consolation, shared the current turmoil in my life. Father Uche listened intently and offered me exactly the comfort and blessing I needed. He truly has a special soul.

Throughout the liturgical celebration, he continued to impress me with his joy and his heartfelt interpretation of Scripture during the homily. I am already looking forward to hearing more of his sermons. Celebrating 14 years of his priesthood, it's easy to see why this parish is so full -- Father Uche fills hearts, minds, and souls with the love and words of Christ. The Deacons and support also do an outstanding job. The Lord is blessing His people with His promises and presence at this church!! Here is proof because the Lord's promise is directly here in this picture I took years ago. So grateful for your beautiful service for this community!! God's Blessings to y'all ✝️ St. Paul the Apostle Catholic Church is truly a cornerstone of the Chino Hills community—a sacred space where open-hearted individuals come together to worship, grow in faith, and feel embraced by something greater. It holds a very special place in my heart, as it’s where my daughter was baptized—a moment I will forever cherish.

The church itself is stunning, with a peaceful beauty that draws you in, but it’s the people who make it truly extraordinary. The parish community is warm, welcoming, and genuinely caring. Whether you’re a lifelong member or visiting for the first time, you’ll be met with kindness and a willingness to serve. St. Paul’s is more than just a church—it’s a spiritual home for anyone seeking connection, love, and purpose.

name: St. Paul's Lutheran Church
St. Paul's Lutheran Church - Pacific Beach Campus
reviewSummary:
Our family’s experience at St. Paul’s Lutheran School in San Diego has been truly exceptional. With three kids enrolled, we see every day how a nurturing environment and strong academics go hand in hand. The teachers genuinely care for each child, and the small class sizes allow for meaningful, personalized attention. What makes St. Paul’s especially unique is the strong sense of family and its Christ-centered foundation. Faith isn’t just taught—it’s lived out daily, shaping our children both academically and spiritually. We are so grateful to be part of this loving community.

That same warmth extends beyond the school and into the church. The congregation is welcoming and kind, and our kids love Sunday Kids Church. There are so many opportunities to get involved—Bingo, school events, house building in Mexico, backpack drives, Bible studies, and gatherings for kids, youth, young adults, women, and men. There truly is something for everyone, and it’s a joy to be part of a church that feels like home. We love our St. Paul's family!
St. Paul's is a welcoming, vibrant community of faith.
The friendships we have made through our church have been lifelong and meaningful.
Pastor Nathan and Pastor Isaac are very personable and available for us as a family.
Their preaching is relatable and easy to apply to our everyday lives!
It has been a great community in which to raise our children.
We highly recommend St. Paul's Lutheran Church! My family loves going to St. Paul’s. I have two year old twins and a 7 year old and this church is very family friendly. If my kids make noises during church no one minds. They all welcome the children and are happy to have them there. They also have a cry room in the back where you can still see and hear the service. My twins love going to the nursery and playing during the sermon. My 7 year old goes with the older kids for the kids sermon and always has fun. It is a warm and welcoming environment. This is a wonderful place to serve with people that are passionate about education in our school and believe in raising up the next generation. This is a congregation that is faithful to the Word of God and also desires to reach the community with the good news of Jesus.

The school music program is a regular blessing to the worship here at St. Paul's. Hope to see you join us in worship of God. I've been attending St. Paul's since my return to San Diego in 2020.  COVID certainly made things challenging at the start, but that's behind us.  Worship experience is great because it's authentic and inviting.  I like that Pastor Hausch and Pastor Davis frequently explain why we worship the way we do...makes it easier for guests to understand.  And then, there's the music.  Our music director does a tremendous job of integrating instruments like strings, brass, and tympani with the organ.  Traditional hymns played a brisk pace so they don't seem like a dirge!  Also, new voices for solos are brought in from time to time, and they're always great. I've made many friends, including the guys that attend the weekly Saturday breakfast at the Broken Yolk in PB.  It's a great time to laugh, share stories about what's going on in our lives, and have some interesting discussions about Jesus and the bible.  Lots of great worship opportunities coming up for Christmas Eve and Christmas Day...come join us!
Mark Ernster

name: St. Paul's Lutheran Church - Santa Monica Campus
reviewSummary: Such a beautiful church in Santa Monica with one of the warmest, kindest, and most welcoming community. I felt so comfortable when I first went and it gave me a feeling of home as an international student. Pastor Jim is wonderful and the choir is amazing. I love going there on Sundays. A worshipping community open to all, committed to justice, service, and peace. A place where love is preached and practiced. Open, warm, inspiring to all people - they embrace you and make you feel loved and at home! Incredible place. Taught me the truth of God’s unconditional love. Love this church and Pastor Jim!

On to HS.  Many memories. Focus on Christ. Need I say more?

name: St. Paul's Lutheran Preschool Long Beach
St. Paul's Lutheran Preschool Long Beach - Long Beach Campus
reviewSummary:
I have two kids who attended St. Paul's over the last ten years. There are too many wonderful things for me to me to be able to list all here. They provided a caring, loving, safe, and fun learning environment. The staff and leadership are wonderful and caring. My two kids are very different from each other, both with their own separate challenges, and they each recieved the appropriate instruction and care for where they were developmentally. I can't imagine having raised our kids without St. Paul's. I am eternally grateful for the role they played in an important stage of our kid's lives. My two children have attended St. Paul’s. My daughter is now in kinder but my son continues to attend the school. My children love St. Paul’s and I do too. The staff is an extension of our family and I know my kids are safe in their care. As a credentialed teacher, I also know that the curriculum is developmentally appropriate. More than anything, the school has always been supportive of my children and their individual needs. St. Paul’s has a special place in family’s heart 🩷 My daughter absolutely thrived at St. Paul’s  Daycare for three years. The staff there became like family, and seeing her happy and excited every day was priceless. From messy art projects to outdoor adventures, she had a blast while learning and making friends. Couldn't have asked for a better start for her. We started St Paul’s unexpectedly early after our son’s prior daycare closed pretty suddenly. We had heard great things from our neighbor so we decided to give them a call in hopes they had a spot for us! Luckily they did. Our son did so well here, his teachers cared for him so much and the director is amazing and very kind and reachable, etc. A mom of young kids herself too which is nice and relatable. They had a lot of fun activities and celebrations, often involving the families. Our son learned a lot and most importantly he worked on his social skills, etc. Our older son had done a CDC for preschool and I wished later that he had done something more like St Paul’s. The CDC turned out to be more academics and a lot less “fun” than I think is appropriate for that age. My youngest is now in TK at a public school after St Pauls and he’s thriving! Our experience with St. Paul’s has been nothing short of exceptional. After trying four different preschools in the Long Beach area, we finally felt at home here. The school has truly become an integral part of our family's journey since enrolling my girls in the Fall of 2021 at 2 and 3 years old.

The teachers and director exemplify the epitome of love, care, and dedication. It's evident from the moment you step through the doors that these educators are not just there to teach, but to nurture and inspire. Their genuine love for the children creates a warm and inviting atmosphere where every child (and parent) feels heard, valued and supported.

For our family, the school curriculum perfectly blends spiritual teaching as well as play-based and didactic education, fostering holistic development in our children. From a short chapel service every Wednesday, to imaginative storytelling sessions and impromptu student led puppet shows, a monthly “share day” where each student gets to shine and hands-on sensory and science experiments, daily activities are thoughtfully designed to ignite learning, curiosity and creativity.

One of the things we appreciate most is how the staff caters to all little personalities and learning types. Whether it's a quiet introvert or a spirited extrovert, each child is encouraged to thrive in their own way. The approachability and relatability of the staff further enhance this nurturing environment, making it easy for both children and parents to feel at home.

Although our older daughter has moved on, the friendships she formed at there have persisted throughout the past year and a half. It speaks volumes about the sense of community fostered. And as for our younger daughter, who was initially shy, she has blossomed into a confident classroom leader in the past 3 years.

The additional services offered, such as extended care and hot lunch three days a week, have been a lifesaver for our family, especially working long shifts in healthcare.

I cannot recommend this school highly enough. It's more than just a preschool; it's a place where children flourish, friendships thrive, and families feel embraced.

name: St. Peter's Episcopal Church - Del Mar Campus
reviewSummary:
I was guest on one service. So nice that they include little kids in regular service, not separate. Woman as a pastor, really wonderful. If you don’t want to be recorded, they have separate seats. Very thoughtful. Their secondhand shop is little gem. A strong message from the pulpit, a lovely historic building with beautiful stained glass, some welcoming faces, and a fun themed summer music series featuring compositions and arrangements from local composers. This is a very welcoming church. Extremely family friendly. Your child can join in the front to watch the Eucharist up close. Every Sunday there is a special children's sermon.  The priest sits on the steps & explains the lesson & children participate. There is a special colorful area with a rug, color crayons,  & paper for the Littles to sit. It has the best Sunday school  program ever, using the child centered program called Godly Play.
The message is always fully understandable & I feel inspired by it. The music is joyful, and it is a very happy place. Came here for a friend's wedding. The venue is beautiful. Everything is made out of wood which gives a very warm feeling. The hosts were very accommodating and helpful. There is enough parking for many people, the church will even give you passes to waive the metered parking fees Occasionally,  when my daughter and her partner travel, I stay at their home and watch the pup. St. Peters is in close proximity to their home. Today God called me to visit the church and I was warmly welcomed by everyone. Rev. Paige  was personable , uplifting and engaging! I also love that they partnered with NAMI, a non profit near and dear to my heart! Thank you and God Bless!

name: St. Petka's Serbian Orthodox Church
St. Petka's Serbian Orthodox Church - San Marcos Campus
reviewSummary:
Very good location, with ample parking, inside the beautiful place for XV party decoration, simply the best option. I shot a quick drone video on my YouTube channel here (Sebastian's Script), and it was beautiful. Only giving 4 stars bc I didn't go inside, otherwise I am certain it would be 5. Calming energy. A very beautiful church, this festival was one of my favorites. The people were so welcoming and warm, the food was exceptional. I really enjoyed myself and tried so hard to go again on Sunday. I will definitely return for future events. Beautiful church! The sanctuary itself is stunning, but what really surprised me was the huge event hall attached that is available for rental. It can be dressed up for just about anything weddings, receptions, banquets. I’m not Serbian Orthodox, but I had the good fortune to attend an event here, and it was wonderful. There’s a spacious cocktail area, a seriously impressive bar, and a large kitchen equipped with stoves and refrigeration that can handle a crowd. You can tell the space was designed with community gatherings in mind.
And speaking of gatherings the annual Serbian Festival in the fall is a can’t-miss. The food is incredible. You can literally smell it as you drive up the hill. Grilled meats, savory pastries, and desserts you’ll dream about afterward. If you’re looking for authentic hospitality and food that makes you close your eyes in happiness, this is the place.
Now, to address the head-scratchers who left negative reviews because they were upset it’s private property: It’s a church, not a public park. Religious sites across the country have had to increase security for obvious reasons, and St. Petka is no exception. Expecting to wander in uninvited for a picnic is like walking into someone’s backyard BBQ and demanding a plate you’ll just look silly. This is a community of faith, and their grounds are for worshippers and invited guests. Respect that, and when you are invited in, you’ll find a warm, welcoming community that knows how to celebrate.
If you’re lucky enough to attend an event here, enjoy it’s a gem. My family moved down from the Bay Area to Oceanside a few years ago and we desperately needed to find an Eastern Orthodox church for worship and fellowship.

After visiting and attending services at numerous area churches we had decided St. Petka in San Marcos met and exceeded all religious needs. The priest Father Milovan is very nice and follows the tradition of the Eastern Orthodox faith and services.

The people are friendly and there is fellowship and lunch after the services in the kitchen hall. The food is highly rated and bountiful for all.

There is a mix of parishioners Serbians, Russians, Greeks, Ukrainians, and other nationalities. All very respectful of each other and very friendly.

My family have found a home in this beautiful cathedral style church and large kitchen and banquet hall facilities. The large banquet hall can be rented and has a large kitchen, a stage, and many banquet style tables which is perfect for a wedding or any celebration.

I highly recommend this beautiful church for all who are seeking to find a new place of worship in the Eastern Orthodox religion.

name: St. Philip Benizi Catholic Church
St. Philip Benizi Catholic Church - Anaheim Campus
reviewSummary: Very modern style church in West Fullerton with the altar in the middle surrounded by pews. Plenty of seats and parking and easy in and out. The priest, deacon, and parishioners were friendly. After mass food and refrescos were sold in the patio outside of the church.  The music was engaging but sometimes overpowered the cantor. Good experience. ⛪️ Wonderful circular church. Multi race congregation. One is greeted and welcomed during the Sunday Mass. The Holy Mass is celebrated in English and Spanish. On the 2nd and 4th Sunday of the month the Holy Mass is celebrated in Indonesian language. I only can come on special occasions due to the distance, for seniors it's hard to drive when it's already dark. Hi do you still have the summer festival every year? I know it’s around this time of month but can’t find anything online about it. I used to live around the corner and loved going every year, I’ll be in town and wanted to take my kids! They ignore my requests to stop mailing me their requests for money. Typical church-they only want your money, they cannot be bothered to STOP sending notices to my aunt who DIED last year, even though I have repeatedly told them to stop. I wrote to the pastor, the office, I've left messages.

reviewSummary: Welcoming Catholic  Church with lots of variety of opportunities to learn, connect, and be inspired in the spiritual faith.  Besides, the regular masses, there are many small faith groups who get together to pray,  learn, connect, and share stories and life journey experiences. Hi.. Beautiful place! We enjoyed the mass!

name: St. Pius V Catholic Church
St. Pius V Catholic Church - Anaheim Campus
reviewSummary:
Attended English mass on a Sunday. The church is spacious and it was packed with people of diverse backgrounds, the choir sang a few Tagalog songs during the service which I really like. The mass was presided by Fr Eric from Alagad ni Maria. Attended Sunday mass at this church during my visit to California. There’s a huge parking lot available for all churchgoers. Upon arrival, I noticed that there were empty tables reserved for selling something. I heard from one of the staff that there will be a fundraising event selling food (in front of the church?)

The altar has a beautiful mosaic backdrop which I heard was donated by a wealthy billionaire.  Most people arrived on time. Solemn singing from the church choir.  The officiating priest had a good message about how to build strong relationships. Wished we could have witnessed the inside of the church, but it was a great mass outside regardless.  Great experience sitting on Father’s Homily, May God Bless, Protect, Let Us All Prosper and Live in Peace & Harmony. This is for the woman who came up to me to ask me to show her my hands while i was praying because she thought i took the bread of christ no i did not im not going to show you my hands mind your own buisness

name: St. Pius X Catholic Church
St. Pius X Catholic Church - Chula Vista Campus
reviewSummary:
A beautiful church and the priest is wonderful! 5 ⭐'s. In my quest to attend mass in all the San Diego County Catholic Churches, I attended St. Pius X Sunday's Spanish mass. We were welcomed and ask to participate from the minute we walked in with the offerings. They also have Knights of Colombus serving here. Plenty of parking and a large hall for celebrations. Wheelchair ♿ access. So far, in my quest, THE BEST. Thanks Father Ernesto Torres. I attended my niece 's baptism with my brother. There was a guy with short black hair and a mustache. I  believe he was a usher. He was very rude to my brother. All of us being Catholics attending a baptism. He should of carried himself as a Catholic in the Lord's house. Really great experience. We are new in the community and we feel welcomed since the first day. The posada was awesome For 15 years, this church was my home. It is where my children grew up in the faith, and it is where we held my son's funeral. I never imagined I would one day be told to leave a place that held so many of my family's most sacred memories.

My experience with the priest was deeply painful. I felt judged instead of welcomed, intimidated instead of encouraged, and ultimately excluded instead of shepherded. I believe a priest should reflect Christ through humility, compassion, patience, and mercy. Sadly, that was not my experience.

I often witnessed interactions that, in my opinion, lacked kindness and pastoral care. Rather than making people feel loved and accepted, I felt many were left feeling uncomfortable or afraid. That is heartbreaking in a place that should be a refuge for those seeking God.

A church should be a place where people encounter grace, healing, and hope—not fear. No priest is above the Gospel he preaches, and actions should reflect the message proclaimed from the altar.

I pray for healing for everyone who has been hurt, including myself. I also pray that this parish will one day become a place where every person is treated with the dignity, compassion, and love that Christ calls us to show one another.

name: St. Rita Catholic Church
St. Rita Catholic Church - San Diego (Downtown) Campus
reviewSummary:
As part of my pilgrimage to visit every Catholic church in San Diego County, I had the pleasure of attending Saint Rita's Sunday morning service. What a gem! Ample parking made arrival a breeze, and the moment I stepped inside, I was enveloped by a warm and inviting atmosphere. The community truly radiated kindness, and I even received a friendly invitation to their Thursday evening Alpha group. The service itself was uplifting and inspiring, leaving me with a renewed sense of peace. But the highlight came afterwards, when the church offered delicious donuts and coffee, fostering a delightful sense of connection among everyone present.

Saint Rita's warm embrace and welcoming spirit truly stood out in my quest. If you're seeking a meaningful and enriching church experience in San Diego County, I highly recommend checking it out! On Sunday, June 19, 2022 St. Rita’s hosted a Juneteenth Mass with Cardinal Robert McElroy, Bishop John Dolan, Bishop Ramon Bejarano, Deacon Booth, Deacon Marvin Threatt, The Knights & Ladies Auxiliary of Peter Claver. Beautiful church good meaningful services. I, unfortunately, was attending my sister's funeral. She was killed in a car accident. I have family throughout San Diego. St Rita Catholic Church happened to be my sister's parish.  The mass was beautiful we have family members who are Mariachis and they were allowed to sing a traditional Spanish Mass. The Church is large enough to allow the 6 ft. separation for preventing the spread of covid-19, which we all did. Everyone wore their face mask and for the most part everyone was respectful and considerate. My family have been parishioners of this church since 1988. A great church, we found a second family with. the church organization. Friendly people, no matter  who you are, they welcome you with open arms. The Pastor and associate pastors are wonderful people, there are  several  choir groups.

name: St. Rita Catholic Community
reviewSummary: A vibrant Catholic community in the Dallas area known for its welcoming parish life and liturgical tradition.

name: St. Robert Bellarmine Church
St. Robert Bellarmine Church - Burbank Campus
reviewSummary:
Attending Mass for the first time at St. Robert Bellarmine Church was more than just a new experience! It felt like stepping into a different rhythm of faith, one that invited reflection in a quieter, more intimate way. I came to accompany my niece, who regularly attends the Friday Mass, and from the moment we walked in, I could sense that this space held something meaningful for her.

The service itself was different from what I’m accustomed to in a traditional Christian Service, yet there was something deeply grounding about that simplicity. It wasn’t crowded, and in fact, she was the only child present, but instead of feeling out of place, she stood out in the most beautiful way. Watching her follow along so naturally, understanding the priest, responding alongside the congregation… it filled me with a quiet sense of pride that’s hard to put into words.

There’s something powerful about seeing faith through the eyes of a child, pure, attentive, and sincere. In that moment, it wasn’t about how different the Mass felt to me, but about the connection she had with it. She wasn’t just attending… she belonged there.

What stayed with me the most wasn’t just the structure of the service, but the feeling of presence, of being part of something sacred, even in its simplicity. It reminded me that faith doesn’t always have to look the same to be meaningful. Sometimes, it’s in those unfamiliar spaces where we witness the most genuine expressions of devotion.

I left that day not only grateful for the experience, but deeply moved by my niece’s example. It became less about my first time there, and more about witnessing a young soul so confidently rooted in her faith. And that, in itself, was a blessing. I've never been to this church. Im from Oxnard CA. I just wanted to express my love for Fr. Marco Ortiz. He was at Santa Clara Church in Oxnard for 6 years before relocating to Burbank. He is one of the best! You have a gem on your hands. Through his homilies, he made me re-establish my love and faith in the Catholic Church. I cant thank him enough and miss him very much. I would love to speak with him again and be able to attend a mass where he is leading. God bless you Fr. Marco, and God bless the Catholic Church. 🙏🏼 🤲🏼 I don't go often bit this is where I have been twice people friendly they greet new comers open heartily. Pastor greets everyone on the way out. Very family oriented It is a very nice church to visit. The choir sings  beautifuly. I love to hear the Christmas Songs always in this holiday season. Definitely will come back again. Beautiful, clean, bright Church, friendly congregation.
Fr. Marco, Dn. Reed, Denise Wilcox and St. Robert Bellarmine staff are very compassionate, caring, dignity and excellence!
God bless St. Robert Bellarmine Church,  Burbank!!!

St. Roch Church - Main Campus
St. Rose of Lima Church
St. Rose of Lima Church - Chula Vista Campus
reviewSummary:
Plain and simple a wonderful and welcoming church. The parking can get full but there’s always a space waiting. The church itself is quite large, the young man I’ve seen play piano and sings leads a beautiful song throughout the service. It’s simple and no fuss and a variety of members- all races sizes of families and even a lot of single people with friendly faces.

I really enjoy their flyer they give On my quest to attend mass in all of the San Diego County Catholic Churches I found another welcoming place to talk to God. The environment is a good place to go to pray and give thanks to our Lord and Savior. I want to visit this church because it is near me. Google always say it is open till 4:30pm but when I get there it is always close. Going around the church to check for an open door just in case but none. Malls, casino, shopping centers are open everywhere but why this kind of establishment is not? Church seeks truth but the ads in google does not. So disappointed! Its a little silly to rate a house God ( a catholic temple) no matter what your experience is with a particular building of the church please do not leave the true church of Christ. Sometimes people within the church are not the friendliest for they are human , but do you walk away from the place that gives you the true body of Christ? I will never. I committed the horrible sin of standing near the door instead of further away, even though it was my first time there and I was just seeking help, not disrespect. Stay away from this place and people who disrespect homeless individuals while claiming to "help" them.

name: St. Simeon Orthodox Church
St. Simeon Orthodox Church - Santa Clarita Campus
reviewSummary: Discovered this church during Easter of 2022 and thank God for that as it was one of the darkest times of my life. With open hands and a smile on their face, people welcomed me and introduced themselves to me and the more I visited the more I started feeling hope for myself and my life. To this day I don't think they know how much they've given me. Thank you God for the St Simeon Orthodox Church! Beautiful Orthodox Church. The Divine Liturgy is in English & the people are very welcoming.  I love the icons here. St. Simeon's is a Christian Church in the Orthodox tradition. It was started in 2013 by an intrepid community of Christ-followers. It has grown over the last few years and found its way to this new location (as of November 2017). Visitors will find welcoming and friendly folks from ages 0 to 80 and beyond. Fr. George is leading the flock in the worship of God and the living out of the Christian life. Great church, friendly people, very new church you can barely notice it from the street Beautiful campus and wonderful staff and church

name: St. Stephen’s Episcopal Church⛪ - Los Angeles (Downtown) Campus
reviewSummary:
St Stephen was highlighted in a powerful segment on CBS Sunday morning today. As an atheist, Im sadden to see the faithful being denied in person  church service because of the fear of being arrested by ICE. What has the United States become? ICE practices are mimicking the Nazi playbook: forcing people to worship in secret, arresting people at churches, hospitals and courthouses. As a son of immigrant parents, I'll always support those in search of a better life here. As a recent transplant SAG actor/singer/musician from NYC,, at my first Sunday AM bi-lingual service at this interesting out of the box church felt welcoming & warm.
Newly ordained priest Holly is to be recognized as terrific addition to the staff at St Stephens.
Blessings to all involved in making this a unique place of worship & community outreach.
Lady Jane Robertson Being an fello Episcopalian. It seems very Inviting: yet; obviously, it Requires a Gated Enterance. Being a Cushion of a Retired, among the 1st Women to be Ordain in NYC, I’m a Custom. It’s like a punk rock church. Kinda, In ethic... But still steeped in the old rituals. Free thinkers and public servants run this church for real public benefit. I like. Bilingual services. I sing and play guitar as a part of a worship team for this church. It's a fantastic church, led by Pastor, Father Jaime, St Stevens Episcapal Church

name: St. Therese of Carmel Catholic Church
St. Therese of Carmel Catholic Church - Del Mar Campus
reviewSummary:
Beautiful Church! Attended Ash Wednesday 5:30 PM service 2/18/26. St Thérèsa of Carmel is my patron saint and I have always wanted to see this parish I’ve heard so many wonderful things about!!
Well they are all true! Rev Christopher Tozzi & Deacon John Fanelle noticed every single visitor! My husband with his walker, Deacon found us & reassured he would personally bring ashes & the Eucharist to him where he sat. The service was beautifully paced, engaging, and pews filled with song books & missiles to use in following along. The energy of the entire church was filled with love & happiness, it was one of the most moving experiences I have had in a long time. The way the pews circle the altar allows for a visual of Father, the readings, and homily to be seen easily, which is important to me!!! I highly recommend visiting St Thérèsa’s in Del Mar it is easy to find right off Interstate 5. I write my review to praise the architecture of this building. You can tell the design is very modern, but that doesn't mean it is barren. It has the perfect balance of ornament and simplicity. There are so many sources of natural light in this church, which improves the atmosphere greatly. I also think the seating arrangement is successful and I have a particular liking to the material chosen for the floor. The highlight must be the large windowed wall that overlooks the surrounding mountainscape. It is a small local church that manages to feel grandiose due to its impressive construction. Overall, 4/5. The architect for this site deserves huge applause! Grounds are unbelievable! The stone throughout, the altar backing up to the mountains, stained glass windows, everything about this church speaks peace and landscaping is a beautiful reflection of St Therese. Pastor's homily was touching. Very happy we came here while on vacation. It's such a beautiful church! The priest and the choir are awesome. The layout and the design of the church are beautiful! Visited this beautiful parish on the very day of the last of papal mass celebrations for our dearly departed Pope Francis.

We were greeted by the most friendly usher, not sure of his name, that honored my family [wife,son,myself] in asking us to bring the gifts to the altar for the liturgy of the Eucharist.

The father gave a beautiful Homily on the life Pope Francis. Overall it was a very welcoming experience that left a good impression on me and my family.

I left the mass feeling renewed and at peace 🕊️

St. Therese Parish - El Cajon Campus
reviewSummary:
Absolutely enchanting~♡ The moment you arrive, everything feels so serene & peaceful. The rose garden is especially stunning~ So many beautiful roses blooming in lovely colors! It feels almost storybook-like and so calming to walk through. ⁠✧⁠*⁠。Mass here is truly beautiful and reverent, filled with such warmth and tranquility. The atmosphere is comforting, prayerful, and deeply uplifting. A truly lovely parish and one of the most beautiful places to spend quiet time with God. ♥️︎ Being here feels so touching as someone who dearly loves Saint Thérèse. (My patron saint) ✿ On my quest to attend mass at every church in San Diego County, I was thrilled to find this welcoming community today. The warm atmosphere and friendly faces truly made me feel at home. The beautiful chorus added a special touch to the service, and the ample parking made the whole experience stress-free. Plus, the church itself is surrounded by stunning scenery, creating a truly peaceful place for reflection. Lord have blessed us with amazing father and staff full of love for our parishioners and community .thank you Jesus Our family and I went here for ash Wednesday for the first time and it was a really nice service and everyone was so friendly 🙏🏾😊 Great church, very welcoming.
Especially the priests . Thank you .

name: St. Thomas Episcopal Church
St. Thomas Episcopal Church - Brea Campus
St. Thomas More Catholic Church
St. Thomas More Catholic Church - Oceanside Campus
reviewSummary:
Incredibly beautiful campus. Beautiful music and meaningful teaching. Come and see and experience the faith of the people. This is our home parish. Love how warm and friendly it is. Fr. Brent, the new pastor is great. Love his Bible Studies. The music ministry is great here as well. This early morning, I stopped before this church — a place I had passed many times over the years, yet only today did something in my heart whisper: pause here.

I now find myself on the threshold of a spiritual journey — inspired by the path of Saint Ignatius of Loyola.

Profound transformations are unfolding within my life, and on this very day, I saw this house of prayer as though Heaven gently unveiled it before me.

I have not yet stepped inside, but already I feel: this may become a sacred home where I can listen intently to the Holy Spirit and open my soul to every word that descends from above.

There is a silence here, filled with light — a stillness that speaks.

With reverence and quiet anticipation,
Alexander My 92 year old uncle had been hospitalized and then brought home to hospice care.  As a devout Catholic he expressed his desire to receive communion.  Messages to St. Thomas requesting a visit from a priest have still yet to be returned. This church is my safe place. Always beautiful services. May the lord continue to bless and guide fr. Brent , fr. Bui and all whom enter this parish. Thank you for being so welcoming.

name: St. Thomas the Apostle
St. Thomas the Apostle - Los Angeles (Downtown) Campus
reviewSummary:
As a non denominational born-again Christian, I thoroughly enjoyed the atmosphere and message of peace preached here. A welcoming church that does a good job of encouraging an appreciation for Christ and His salvation for the world. As someone who recently moved to this neighborhood & is in their early 30s, I’ve really grown to love it here. Father Davies is kind, friendly, & welcoming, & I always look forward to his lectures—they’re my favorite part of Sunday mass. The place itself is beautiful, & I think I’ve found my second home. Highly recommended! This is a very welcoming place.  Everything seems to be in place.  There is a great sermon, a sermon that keeps you thinking the whole week.  Father Davies is amazing !! He takes the time to greet each one of the parishioners at the end of mass.  This is a place where progressive thinking and traditional worship joint in the most perfect "divine" way.  I would really recommend this place to get to know the Episcopal church, they accept you as you are.  You will mature in faith by coming and sharing faith and actions.  They have a couple of active ministries for AIDS, homeless, etc.  You will enjoy your time here.  Come and visit this amazing home of God. St. Thomas the Apostle church is one of the most soul-enriching experiences I have known in Los Angeles.  From the parish to the members and the congregation and the choir, I've never met anyone who didn't make me feel welcomed and included here.  They provide outreach and community support and education programs as well as spiritual support.  Whether you are visiting the city or looking for a new place of worship or perhaps in search of community, you will not be disappointed. Welcome one, welcome all...St Thomas welcomes the Choir back for Sacred Mass! I was all smiles by the time I left.

As of 2/20/22 masks are still worn per county guidelines 😷

This High-Episcopal church has a very contemplative service with "smells & bells", incense that is... :-)

St. Thomas the Apostle Catholic Church - Los Angeles (Downtown) Campus
reviewSummary: Women on the phone was not helpful at all. Called for times for event didn’t want to help out at all. They have a Beautiful Pieta outside of the church. I went to see The Virgen Mary and gift her with these Roses in honor of my Beloved. My mom has been very sick and she's been wanting to assist to Sunday's mass in person at the mentioned place. My dear mom was very happy, joyful and overwhelmed for being abled that finally did  it. You can't imagine how happy I feel, she's 90 years old,  I thank My dear God dailyfor every thing, He bless us. Thank you very much. Blessings to all. St. Thomas the Apostle Catholic Church provides a warm, faith-filled environment with meaningful Masses, friendly parishioners, and strong community support. Truly uplifting and welcoming. Beautiful procession for the relics of Saint Carlo Acutis, at St. Thomas.

name: St. Thomas the Apostle Catholic Church - Riverside Campus
reviewSummary:
Me and my family incredibly blessed to have Father Ted at Saint Thomas Parish.
He is, without question, the best priest our community has ever had -- and we mean that from the bottom of our hearts.
His homilies speak to us in a way that is warm, meaningful, and deeply personal.
Every word he shares carries love, wisdom, and grace. The faithful truly look forward to every Mass because of the spirit and joy he brings to our church.
We are so happy and grateful that Father Ted is still with us, and our prayer is that he remains at Saint Thomas for many more years to come. His presence is a true gift to this parish and to everyone who walks through these doors.
Thank you, Father Ted -- for your kindness, your dedication, and your beautiful heart. You are simply the best! PLEASE READ. I attended Easter 7AM mass this morning. It’s a lovely church and parishioners seemed nice but there are a few things that I would like to address that bothered me.

1. People showing up late. A common problem in our society today. There was a time when people came on time. My mom tells me that when she was going to church as a girl when mass started doors were closed. If someone came 5-10 minutes late the doors were locked. Today I saw quite a few people come in late. A rule should be enforced that if people are late and mass has already begun they should be advised to come to next mass. The next mass today would have been 9:00 am. I was by myself but today 5 minutes after mass had started 3 people came in and squeezed themselves next to me. Needless to say I felt cramped since the 2 people in particular were larger people. They all had time to prepare for mass to start. They knew ahead of time. Come early or don’t come at all. Churches as we all know depend heavily on financial support from its parishioners. Maybe if the powers at be would be more stricter in enforcing some of these rules it might deter people from coming. Well that’s their choice. Better to have fewer parishioners than a multitude who don’t respect schedules.

2. I got there 40 minutes early and was trying to pray and some of the ushers were greeting each other. I have no problem with that of course however they weren’t talking in hushed tones. It was hard for me to concentrate. They were more than old enough to know to be quiet 🤫. Some of us are trying to meditate.

3. The Father. He seemed like a nice man and praises God in his own unique way but I could barely understand what he was saying. I don’t know how long he’s been here in the USA but if he’s been here for any length of time he should be able to speak better English. I got some of what he said but it was obvious he had no sermon prepared. I find that many foreign language speakers who have to talk take shortcuts when they do speak so they don’t have to talk very long if that makes sense. They say the same thing repeatedly but just differently. Father needs to start preparing his speeches ahead of time. He does it extemporaneously. Few people are capable of doing that and get their point across. 5 minutes into her sermon and I had no idea what he was talking about. Language barrier for sure. I like to hear what people especially an ordained member of the clergy on what they’re saying.

4. Last and final thing. I do wish people would dress up more at Easter. Heck people don’t dress for anything anymore. The Wales 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁷󠁬󠁳󠁿 Family and all Royal families in Europe really know how to dress. The British royal family especially could teach Americans a thing or to about tradition and how to dress appropriately for mass. Just saying. Don’t believe me look it up on Twitter or “X.” If this bothered anyone reading this well all due respect not my problem.

In closing lovely church, great people, but some changes need to be made like appropriate attire from the parishioners, showing up to mass ON TIME. If you can be on time for work then you can be on time for Church. Beautiful Catholic Church

Father Ted is a great pastor/farther

And father Celestine 🇻🇦.

Whether in USA, Mexico, Japan or anywhere in the world its a blessing we can always find a catholic church.

reviewSummary: My 1.5 and 4 year old love worship in the kids ministry and always come home singing the songs from the mornings’ worship time. I understand how to read the Bible, relate to people who are different than me, and how to have a relationship with God so much more because of the sermons at Stone Arbor. name: Story Church
Story Church - Rancho Cucamonga Campus
reviewSummary:
Our family loves Story Church and our church community! We’ve had the privilege of being members of the church since the beginning and seeing our kids grow up in this church has been such a blessing! The children’s ministry is amazing! Our boys have grown so much in their faith and I know that Story has played a huge part in this. We’re forever grateful for the hardworking staff and volunteers that make it a priority to teach our kids the truth of the gospel week after week! We've been attending Story Church for more than 5 years now and love it. It has been amazing to see this new church plant grow and reach so many people in the community with the gospel. They have a great children's program for kids ages 1 til 5th grade, and a youth program for students in 6th-12th grade. There's "home groups" that meet throughout the week, making it easy to get connected well with different people. And now that they're in a new building that they have access to all week, they now offer various programs like women's Bible study, men's discipleship groups, classes, prayer meetings, and more. We love Story Church and have been so blessed by the Bible-based preaching, the people, the worship teams, our home group, the kids' programs, serving in various roles, and more! We started attending Story after my friend prompted us to. I kept telling her I didn't want to come to some new "hipster church." Our first service was a Christmas Eve service right before the pandemic hit and I was instantly drawn in.

Solid, Bible based preaching, a warm and welcoming community for our kids (and a kids ministry that really focuses on teaching our kids, not just babysitting), godly leadership, and a desire to really see one another grow in our faith.

We recently attended the membership class and I'm very grateful for the checks and balances that are in place to hold those who are shepherding us accountable.

I've grown up in church my whole life and I've been in churches where 10% of the people do all the work to keep things going. Story church also has protocols in place for those who serve so that they are not just always serving but are also in service getting fed as well.

Our community group is extremely diverse when it comes to age, marital status, having kids, etc but it has been so wonderful to have that small group community to dig deeper into life with.

I'm thankful to be a part of this body of believers. We love Story Church!  It’s a place where the gospel is preached, the Bible is taught, and the Spirit is active.   It’s a place where the broken find forgiveness and transformation and people from all backgrounds find a home in the family of God. Solid Gospel-centered preaching church. We’ve called it home for the past 6 years👍🏼
